objects.description: Opaque handle for a platform-specific monotonic timer used with evutil_configure_monotonic_time() and evutil_gettime_monotonic(). Allocate with evutil_monotonic_timer_new() and free with evutil_monotonic_timer_free(). Internal layout is intentionally hidden.

Libevent-provided replacement for struct addrinfo on platforms lacking it. Mirrors POSIX getaddrinfo fields; instances are produced by evutil_getaddrinfo() and must be released with evutil_freeaddrinfo().

Opaque buffer type used by libevent for efficient byte storage and I/O. Only a forward declaration appears in this header; definition is elsewhere. Used here as the container for marshaling and unmarshaling tagged data.
Unsigned 32-bit integer typedef imported from event2/util.h. Used for tag identifiers and 32-bit payload integers. Defined in an external header; not defined here.
Unsigned 64-bit integer typedef imported from event2/util.h. Used for 64-bit payload integers. Defined in an external header; not defined here.
POSIX time interval structure referenced here for marshaling/unmarshaling time values. Only referenced; definition is in system headers.

Opaque handle for a Libevent dispatch loop. Tracks pending/active events, runs their callbacks. Allocate with event_base_new() or event_base_new_with_config(); free with event_base_free() or event_base_free_nofinalize(). Only one thread may dispatch a given base at a time.

Opaque structure representing a single event (fd readiness, signal, timeout, or user-trigger). Create with event_new() or assign with event_assign(); add with event_add(); remove with event_del(); free with event_free(). Supports flags like EV_READ, EV_WRITE, EV_SIGNAL, EV_PERSIST, EV_ET, EV_FINALIZE, EV_CLOSED.

Opaque configuration object used to influence creation of an event_base (backend selection, feature requirements, flags, dispatch tuning). Allocate with event_config_new(); free with event_config_free().
Bitmask enum describing features supported/required by an event backend. Used with event_config_require_features() and event_base_get_features(). Pointer form rarely used; values are OR-able flags.
Bitmask enum of configuration flags affecting event_base behavior and backend specifics. Used via event_config_set_flag(). Pointer form seldom used directly; values are OR-able.
Function pointer type for receiving Libevent log messages. Install with event_set_log_callback().
Function pointer type invoked on fatal internal Libevent errors. Install with event_set_fatal_callback().
Callback prototype for struct event. Arguments: fd/signal, bitmask of EV_* triggers, and user arg.
Callback prototype for event finalization helpers event_finalize() and event_free_finalize(). Called from the loop when the event is safe to tear down.

objects.definition: typedef int (*event_base_foreach_event_cb)(const struct event_base *, const struct event *, void *);
objects.description: Callback prototype used with event_base_foreach_event() to iterate over added/active events. Return 0 to continue, nonzero to stop.

Opaque buffer object used for efficient network I/O buffering. Created with evbuffer_new() and freed with evbuffer_free(). Many API functions operate on it (add, remove, peek, freeze, etc.). Internals are hidden; treat as opaque.

Iterator-like position within an evbuffer for searching/peeking. Must only be manipulated via evbuffer_ptr_set(); invalidated by buffer modifications or repacking. Can represent positions from start up to just after end.

aliases: evbuffer_iovec * (macro alias to iovec when native)
objects.description: Describes an extent of memory inside an evbuffer for zero-copy style access in reserve/commit/peek APIs. When sys/uio.h is available, it aliases the native struct iovec; otherwise a compatible struct is defined here.
Enumeration of end-of-line parsing styles for evbuffer_readln() and evbuffer_search_eol(). Controls which byte sequences are recognized as line terminators.

Opaque handle to a file-backed data segment that can be inserted into an evbuffer (zero-copy via sendfile/mmap where available). Created with evbuffer_file_segment_new() and freed with evbuffer_file_segment_free(); lifetime is reference-counted across buffers.
How to adjust an evbuffer_ptr with evbuffer_ptr_set(): either set absolute position or add relative offset.
Information passed to evbuffer callbacks describing size changes since the last invocation.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*evbuffer_ref_cleanup_cb)(const void *data,
    size_t datalen, void *extra);
objects.description: Function pointer type for cleanup of memory regions referenced by an evbuffer via evbuffer_add_reference[_with_offset](). Called when the referenced region is no longer used.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*evbuffer_file_segment_cleanup_cb)(
    struct evbuffer_file_segment const* seg, int flags, void* arg);
objects.description: Function pointer type for cleanup notifications on evbuffer_file_segment when all references are gone.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evbuffer_cb_func)(struct evbuffer *buffer, const struct evbuffer_cb_info *info, void *arg);
objects.description: Callback function type invoked when data is added to or removed from an evbuffer. Receives the buffer, change info, and user arg.
Opaque handle representing a registered evbuffer callback instance, returned by evbuffer_add_cb() and used to manage flags or removal.
Opaque handle representing a buffered I/O object with input/output evbuffers and callbacks. Actual structure is hidden; only a forward declaration is provided here.
Function pointer type for read/write data callbacks invoked when input has data past low watermark or output drains below low watermark.

objects.definition: typedef void (*bufferevent_event_cb)(struct bufferevent *bev, short what, void *ctx);
objects.description: Function pointer type for event/error callbacks invoked on EOF, errors, timeouts, or successful connect events; ‘what’ is a bitmask of BEV_EVENT_* flags.
Bitflag options used when creating bufferevents to control lifecycle, locking, and callback deferral/unlocking behavior.
Indicates how aggressively filters/bufferevents should process/flush data: normal, flush pending data, or finish at end-of-stream.
Flags modifying behavior of bufferevent_trigger and bufferevent_trigger_event: ignore watermarks or defer callbacks.
Return codes for filter callbacks: successfully produced output, need more input, or encountered an unrecoverable error.
Function pointer type for filter transforms between source and destination evbuffers with an optional output limit and flush mode.
Opaque configuration object for per-bufferevent and group rate limiting (token bucket parameters). Only forward-declared here.
Opaque handle for a group of bufferevents sharing aggregate rate limits for read/write throughput.

Opaque listener handle for accepting incoming TCP connections within libevent. The struct is forward-declared only in this header; its layout is private to the library. Instances are created via evconnlistener_new() or evconnlistener_new_bind(), and freed with evconnlistener_free(). Enable/disable and callbacks are managed with the provided API. Internal representation and any invariants are unknown from this header.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evconnlistener_cb)(struct evconnlistener *, evutil_socket_t, struct sockaddr *, int socklen, void *);
objects.description: Function-pointer type for the accept callback invoked when a new connection is received. Parameters: listener, accepted socket fd, peer address pointer, address length, and user argument. The callback may be NULL to keep the listener disabled until set.
Function-pointer type for the error callback invoked on non-retriable listener errors. Parameters: listener and user argument.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evdns_callback_type) (int result, char type, int count, int ttl, void *addresses, void *arg);
objects.description: Function-pointer type for asynchronous DNS query callbacks. Called with result/status, record type, count, TTL, a type-dependent addresses pointer, and user arg.
Function-pointer type for receiving evdns log messages; set via evdns_set_log_fn.
Function-pointer type for implementing a DNS server request handler. Receives a request object and user data.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evdns_getaddrinfo_cb)(int result, struct evutil_addrinfo *res, void *arg);
objects.description: Function-pointer type for nonblocking getaddrinfo results. Receives error code, result list, and user arg.
Opaque handle representing an evdns resolver base associated with an event_base. Created with evdns_base_new and freed with evdns_base_free.
Opaque handle for an in-flight DNS resolution request returned by evdns_base_resolve_* APIs. Can be canceled via evdns_cancel_request.
Opaque object representing an incoming DNS request to a server. Used to build and send replies or drop requests.
Opaque object representing a single question within a DNS server request. Its structure is not exposed here.
Opaque handle for a DNS server port (UDP or TCP). Created by evdns_add_server_port_with_base or evdns_add_server_port_with_listener; closed with evdns_close_server_port.
Enum of configurable options for an evdns TCP server port: maximum concurrent clients and idle timeout (seconds).
Opaque handle for an asynchronous getaddrinfo operation returned by evdns_getaddrinfo; cancelable via evdns_getaddrinfo_cancel until callback fires.

Holds information about an HTTP extended method for use with the extended-method comparison callback. Fields map between textual method name, its bitmask type (from evhttp_cmd_type), and flags (e.g., EVHTTP_METHOD_HAS_BODY).

objects.definition:
enum evhttp_cmd_type {
	EVHTTP_REQ_GET     = 1 << 0,
	EVHTTP_REQ_POST    = 1 << 1,
	EVHTTP_REQ_HEAD    = 1 << 2,
	EVHTTP_REQ_PUT     = 1 << 3,
	EVHTTP_REQ_DELETE  = 1 << 4,
	EVHTTP_REQ_OPTIONS = 1 << 5,
	EVHTTP_REQ_TRACE   = 1 << 6,
	EVHTTP_REQ_CONNECT = 1 << 7,
	EVHTTP_REQ_PATCH   = 1 << 8,
	EVHTTP_REQ_PROPFIND= 1 << 9,
	EVHTTP_REQ_PROPPATCH=1 << 10,
	EVHTTP_REQ_MKCOL   = 1 << 11,
	EVHTTP_REQ_LOCK    = 1 << 12,
	EVHTTP_REQ_UNLOCK  = 1 << 13,
	EVHTTP_REQ_COPY    = 1 << 14,
	EVHTTP_REQ_MOVE    = 1 << 15,
};
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration of supported HTTP methods, including standard and WebDAV/PATCH methods. Used as flags to indicate allowed/requested method types.
Distinguishes whether an evhttp_request object represents an incoming request or an outgoing response context.
Enumeration of error conditions that may occur for an evhttp_request; delivered to error callbacks.
Opaque handle for a parsed URI/relative-ref per RFC3986. The actual structure is private to the library; manage via the provided API to create, modify, query, join, and free.
Callback function type used by evhttp_foreach_bound_socket to iterate over all bound sockets of an evhttp server. The function must not free or remove sockets/listeners during iteration.
Callback type used to translate between extended HTTP method strings and their type/flags. Should set fields on evhttp_ext_method and return 0 on success, -1 on unknown/unsupported method.

objects.definition:
EVRPC_STRUCT(rpcname) { \
	struct evrpc_hook_meta *hook_meta; \
	struct reqstruct* request; \
	struct rplystruct* reply; \
	struct evrpc* rpc; \
	struct evhttp_request* http_req; \
	struct evbuffer* rpc_data; \
};
objects.description: Per-RPC request context structure generated by EVRPC_HEADER for a specific RPC name. Holds hook metadata, pointers to the generated request and reply message objects, owning evrpc, underlying HTTP request, and the encoded RPC payload buffer. The actual concrete name depends on the rpcname used with EVRPC_HEADER: struct evrpc_req__<rpcname>.
Opaque handle for an RPC connection pool used to dispatch client RPCs over one or more evhttp_connection objects. Created and freed via API; contents are intentionally hidden.
Opaque generic RPC request object used internally for server-side request handling and completion. Accessed via helper APIs to retrieve request/reply payloads or to mark completion.
Opaque context object representing a pending client RPC request, including callbacks and (un)marshalling functions. Created by evrpc_make_request_ctx and used with evrpc_make_request.
Opaque descriptor for a registered RPC on the server. Used with low-level registration APIs.
Forward-declared HTTP request object from libevent HTTP layer. Only referenced here; not defined in this header. Details unknown within this file.
Forward-declared status object passed to RPC callbacks to indicate completion state. Definition is external to this header; details unknown here.
Opaque metadata container used by RPC hooks to attach key/value data to a request context. Forward-declared here; structure details are not provided in this header.
Opaque RPC server base that binds RPC handling to an evhttp server instance. Created with evrpc_init and freed with evrpc_free.
Forward-declared libevent HTTP server object referenced when initializing RPC base. Not defined in this header.
Forward-declared HTTP connection handle for client-side pooling. Only referenced; not defined here.
Enumeration selecting whether a hook applies to incoming (EVRPC_INPUT) or outgoing (EVRPC_OUTPUT) processing. Deprecated aliases INPUT/OUTPUT may map to these on non-Windows platforms.
Enumeration of possible outcomes from a hook callback: terminate processing, continue immediately, or pause until explicitly resumed via evrpc_resume_request().

Locking callbacks interface that a threading backend provides to Libevent. It specifies how to allocate, free, lock, and unlock locks, and which lock types are supported. Must be installed via evthread_set_lock_callbacks() before creating any event_base. Details beyond the function signatures are not provided here.

Condition-variable callbacks interface that a threading backend provides to Libevent. It specifies how to allocate, free, signal, and wait on condition variables. Must be installed via evthread_set_condition_callbacks() before creating any event_base. The actual condition and lock objects are opaque void pointers to backend-defined types.
Opaque forward declaration of the Libevent event loop base. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; full definition is elsewhere. Used here for evthread_make_base_notifiable().
Opaque event loop base type from libevent. Only forward-declared here; no definition in this header. Represents the event loop context that owns watchers.
Opaque watcher handle used to register "prepare" and "check" callbacks with an event_base. Forward declaration only in this header.
Opaque context information passed to evwatch_prepare_cb. Forward-declared here; concrete fields are not exposed in this header.
Opaque context information passed to evwatch_check_cb. Forward-declared here; concrete fields are not exposed in this header.
POSIX time interval structure; only forward-declared here to avoid pulling in system headers. Definition is not provided in this header.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evwatch_prepare_cb)(struct evwatch *, const struct evwatch_prepare_cb_info *, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for "prepare" watcher callbacks invoked just before polling for I/O within event_base_loop.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evwatch_check_cb)(struct evwatch *, const struct evwatch_check_cb_info *, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for "check" watcher callbacks invoked immediately after polling and before dispatching active events within event_base_loop.

Opaque handle representing a WebSocket connection/session. This header only provides a forward declaration; the structure layout is hidden. Instances are created by evws_new_session() and should be closed with evws_close() and eventually freed with evws_connection_free().

objects.definition:
typedef void (*ws_on_msg_cb)(
	struct evws_connection *, int type, const unsigned char *, size_t, void *);
objects.description: Function pointer type for the message callback invoked when a WebSocket frame is received. Parameters: evws_connection*, frame type (WS_TEXT_FRAME or WS_BINARY_FRAME), pointer to payload bytes, payload length, and user context pointer. The callback does not take ownership of the data buffer; for text frames the user must ensure NUL-termination if treating as C string.
Function pointer type for a connection-close callback. Invoked when the WebSocket connection is closing/closed, with the connection pointer and the user-provided context.

objects.definition: typedef void (*evbuffer_cb)(struct evbuffer *buffer, size_t old_len, size_t new_len, void *arg);
objects.description: Function-pointer typedef for an evbuffer callback that is invoked whenever data is added to or removed from a struct evbuffer. The callback receives the buffer, the previous length, the new length, and a user-supplied argument. Note: struct evbuffer is only referenced here; it is not defined in this header.
Function pointer type alias used for bufferevent data callbacks. This header only defines a preprocessor alias evbuffercb to bufferevent_data_cb; the actual typedef is not defined here.
Function pointer type alias used for bufferevent event/error callbacks. This header only defines a preprocessor alias everrorcb to bufferevent_event_cb; the actual typedef is not defined here.
Opaque bufferevent structure representing a buffered I/O event. This header references the type and declares functions returning/accepting it, but does not define the struct layout here.
Opaque forward declaration for the asynchronous DNS base object used by deprecated, global-scope DNS APIs. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; the full definition lives elsewhere.
Forward declaration of IPv4 address structure (normally provided by system headers). Only declared here for parameter typing; not defined in this header.
Forward declaration of IPv6 address structure (normally provided by system headers). Only declared here for parameter typing; not defined in this header.

Opaque server-port handle for a DNS server listener used by libevent's deprecated global DNS APIs. It is only referenced via return type of evdns_add_server_port; no struct definition is provided here.

Opaque event loop base type from Libevent. It is only forward-referenced here via function prototypes; the actual struct definition is not present in this header. This type represents the state and backend of the event loop. Details are unknown in this file.

Time interval structure from system headers (sys/time.h). It is referenced as a parameter type in this header but not defined here; therefore, it should generally be treated as an external system type. Included only because it appears in signatures; no construction info in this header.

Opaque HTTP server handle type referenced by this header. It is only forward-declared elsewhere; this header does not define its layout. Used as the return type for evhttp_start, which creates a new HTTP server instance.

Opaque HTTP client/server connection handle referenced by this header. Only forward-declared elsewhere; this header does not define its layout. Created by evhttp_connection_new and can be associated with an event_base via evhttp_connection_set_base.
Opaque libevent event loop base type referenced by this header. Not defined here. It can be associated with an evhttp_connection using evhttp_connection_set_base.
No structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined in this header. It only defines preprocessor macros for backward-compatible RPC accessors. Therefore, there are no custom data types to document.
Placeholder for the libevent DNS base type. This header does not define it; it is included from <event2/dns_struct.h>. Details unknown here.
Opaque handle for an outstanding DNS request. Not defined in this header; provided by <event2/dns_struct.h>. Details unknown here.
Opaque server port object for implementing a DNS server. Not defined in this header; provided by <event2/dns_struct.h>. Details unknown here.
Opaque request object delivered to a DNS server callback. Not defined in this header; provided by <event2/dns_struct.h>. Details unknown here.
Opaque handle for an asynchronous getaddrinfo request. Not defined in this header; provided by <event2/dns_struct.h>. Details unknown here.
Function-pointer type for DNS resolution callbacks. Not defined here; declared in included headers. Details unknown in this header.

functions.name: evutil_date_rfc1123
functions.signature: int evutil_date_rfc1123(char *date, const size_t datelen, const struct tm *tm);
functions.description: Formats a calendar time as an RFC 1123-compliant date string (commonly used in HTTP). If tm is NULL, the current system time is used. Returns the number of characters written; compare this value against datelen to detect truncation.
requirements: date must point to a writable buffer of at least datelen bytes.
datelen should be large enough for an RFC1123 date (recommend >= 30 bytes).
tm may be NULL to use current time; otherwise must point to a valid struct tm.
Callers should check if return value < datelen to ensure the output was not truncated.

functions.name: evutil_monotonic_timer_new
functions.description: Allocates a new opaque monotonic timer object to be used with monotonic-time APIs. Must be configured via evutil_configure_monotonic_time() before retrieving time with evutil_gettime_monotonic().
requirements: The returned pointer must be freed with evutil_monotonic_timer_free().
Timer must be configured with evutil_configure_monotonic_time() before use with evutil_gettime_monotonic().

functions.name: evutil_monotonic_timer_free
functions.description: Frees a monotonic timer previously allocated by evutil_monotonic_timer_new().
requirements: timer must have been returned by evutil_monotonic_timer_new().
Do not use timer after this call.

functions.name: evutil_configure_monotonic_time
functions.description: Initializes a monotonic timer with the given flags. Supported flags include EV_MONOT_PRECISE and EV_MONOT_FALLBACK. Must be called before evutil_gettime_monotonic().
requirements: timer must be a valid pointer returned by evutil_monotonic_timer_new().
Call this before evutil_gettime_monotonic() on the same timer.
flags may include EV_MONOT_PRECISE and/or EV_MONOT_FALLBACK.

functions.name: evutil_gettime_monotonic
functions.description: Retrieves the current monotonic time using a previously configured timer. Monotonic time never goes backward and is suitable for measuring elapsed time; it is not tied to epoch time. Not safe to call concurrently on the same timer from multiple threads.
requirements: timer must have been configured successfully with evutil_configure_monotonic_time().
tp must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable struct timeval.
Do not use the same timer from multiple threads simultaneously.

functions.name: evutil_socketpair
functions.signature: int evutil_socketpair(int domain, int type, int protocol, evutil_socket_t sv[2]);
functions.description: Creates a pair of connected sockets. On Unix, wraps socketpair(). On Windows, uses AF_UNIX if available or a loopback TCP pair otherwise. EVUTIL_SOCK_NONBLOCK and/or EVUTIL_SOCK_CLOEXEC may be ORed into type to apply to both sockets.
requirements: sv must point to an array of two evutil_socket_t elements.
domain, type, and protocol must be valid for socketpair() on the platform.
May fail on some Windows systems due to loopback restrictions (firewall).

functions.name: evutil_make_socket_nonblocking
functions.description: Applies platform-specific operations to set a socket into nonblocking mode.
requirements: sock must be a valid open socket handle.

functions.name: evutil_make_listen_socket_reuseable
functions.description: Adjusts platform-specific options to allow a listener’s address to be rebound soon after the listener is closed (semantics differ from Windows’s SO_REUSEADDR).
requirements: sock should be a listener socket or a socket intended to be used as a listener.

functions.name: evutil_make_listen_socket_reuseable_port
functions.description: Enables port-level reuse so multiple programs that also set this option can bind/listen on the same port and have incoming connections/datagrams distributed. Available only on specified OS versions (Linux 3.9+, DragonFlyBSD 3.6+, FreeBSD 12.0+, Solaris 11.4, AIX 7.2.5).
requirements: sock should be a listener socket or a socket intended to be used as a listener.
Feature availability depends on OS; returns -1 on failure.

functions.name: evutil_make_listen_socket_ipv6only
functions.description: Sets IPV6_V6ONLY on a listener to accept only IPv6 (i.e., disables IPv4-mapped behavior).
requirements: sock should be a listener socket bound to an IPv6 address.

functions.name: evutil_make_listen_socket_not_ipv6only
functions.description: Clears IPV6_V6ONLY on a listener to allow both IPv6 and IPv4-mapped connections (dual-stack where supported).
requirements: sock should be a listener socket bound to an IPv6 address.

functions.name: evutil_make_socket_closeonexec
functions.description: Marks a socket to be automatically closed on successful exec*() calls (sets close-on-exec or equivalent).
requirements: sock must be a valid open socket handle.

functions.name: evutil_closesocket
functions.description: Performs the appropriate platform-specific call to close a socket obtained from socket() or accept(). Returns 0 on success (even if the operation is a no-op on the platform), -1 on failure.
requirements: sock must be a valid socket handle; behavior is undefined if called twice on the same socket.

functions.name: evutil_make_tcp_listen_socket_deferred
functions.description: Configures a TCP listening socket to defer accept() until data is ready to read, where supported. Useful for protocols where clients speak first. Returns 0 on success whether or not the underlying platform supports the feature; -1 on failure.
requirements: sock must be a TCP listening socket.
Only use for protocols where the client sends data first.

functions.name: evutil_set_tcp_keepalive
functions.signature: int evutil_set_tcp_keepalive(evutil_socket_t sock, int on, int timeout);
functions.description: Enables or disables TCP keep-alive and sets keepalive parameters (TCP_KEEPIDLE, TCP_KEEPINTVL, TCP_KEEPCNT) where supported. timeout specifies the idle time in seconds before the first probe.
requirements: sock must be a TCP socket.
on nonzero enables keep-alive; 0 disables it.
timeout is the idle period in seconds before the first probe (used when enabling).

functions.name: evutil_strtoll
functions.signature: ev_int64_t evutil_strtoll(const char *s, char **endptr, int base);
functions.description: Parses a signed 64-bit integer from a string, with behavior analogous to strtol/strtoll. base selects the numeric base.
requirements: s must be a non-NULL C string.
endptr may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the address of the first unparsed character.
base should be 0 or between 2 and 36, as with standard strto* functions.

functions.name: evutil_gettimeofday
functions.description: Provides gettimeofday functionality. On platforms lacking gettimeofday(), this function is provided; otherwise evutil_gettimeofday is a macro to gettimeofday().
requirements: tv must be a non-NULL pointer to struct timeval to receive the time.
tz may be NULL or a valid pointer to struct timezone, depending on platform (typically unused).

functions.name: evutil_snprintf
functions.signature: int evutil_snprintf(char *buf, size_t buflen, const char *format, ...);
functions.description: A snprintf replacement with consistent C99-conforming return semantics across platforms. Supports printf-style formatting.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of length buflen.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
Variadic arguments must match the format string.

functions.name: evutil_vsnprintf
functions.signature: int evutil_vsnprintf(char *buf, size_t buflen, const char *format, va_list ap);
functions.description: A vsnprintf replacement with consistent C99-conforming return semantics across platforms. Supports printf-style formatting using a va_list.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer of length buflen.
format must be a valid printf-style format string.
ap must be an initialized va_list corresponding to format.

functions.name: evutil_inet_ntop
functions.signature: const char *evutil_inet_ntop(int af, const void *src, char *dst, size_t len);
functions.description: Replacement for inet_ntop. Converts a network address from binary form to presentation (text) form. src must not be NULL.
requirements: af must be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
src must be non-NULL and point to an address of the type indicated by af.
dst must point to a buffer of at least len bytes; len must be large enough for the textual address (recommend INET_ADDRSTRLEN or INET6_ADDRSTRLEN).

functions.name: evutil_inet_pton_scope
functions.signature: int evutil_inet_pton_scope(int af, const char *src, void *dst, unsigned *indexp);
functions.description: Variation of inet_pton that also parses IPv6 scope identifiers (e.g., interface indexes). Public for unit tests; typical applications should not need to call this directly.
requirements: af must be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
src should be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string containing a textual IP address (may include scope for IPv6).
dst must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for the parsed binary address.
indexp, when non-NULL and af is AF_INET6 with a scoped address, may receive the parsed scope index.

functions.name: evutil_inet_pton
functions.signature: int evutil_inet_pton(int af, const char *src, void *dst);
functions.description: Replacement for inet_pton. Converts an IPv4/IPv6 address from presentation (text) to network (binary) form. src must not be NULL.
requirements: af must be AF_INET or AF_INET6.
src must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string containing the textual IP address.
dst must be a non-NULL pointer to storage for the parsed binary address.

functions.name: evutil_parse_sockaddr_port
functions.signature: int evutil_parse_sockaddr_port(const char *str, struct sockaddr *out, int *outlen);
functions.description: Parses an IPv4 or IPv6 address with optional port from a string. Supports "[v6]:port", "[v6]", "v6", "v4:port", and "v4". If no port is present, the port in the result is set to 0. On success, writes the address to out and sets *outlen to the number of bytes used.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL string in one of the recognized formats.
out must point to a writable struct sockaddr buffer (struct sockaddr_storage recommended).
outlen must be a non-NULL pointer; on input, *outlen must contain the capacity in bytes of out; on success, *outlen is updated to the size used.
Returns -1 if the address is malformed, the port is out of range, or out is too small.

functions.name: evutil_sockaddr_cmp
functions.signature: int evutil_sockaddr_cmp(const struct sockaddr *sa1, const struct sockaddr *sa2, int include_port);
functions.description: Compares two socket addresses. Returns 0 if equal, <0 if sa1 precedes sa2, >0 if sa1 follows sa2. If include_port is nonzero, the port is included in the comparison. Implemented for AF_INET and AF_INET6 only; ordering is not stable across libevent versions.
requirements: sa1 and sa2 must be non-NULL and point to valid AF_INET or AF_INET6 sockaddrs.
include_port should be 0 or nonzero to indicate whether ports are considered.

functions.name: evutil_ascii_strcasecmp
functions.description: Case-insensitive string compare in a locale-independent ASCII manner (unaffected by current locale).
requirements: str1 and str2 must not be NULL.

functions.name: evutil_ascii_strncasecmp
functions.signature: int evutil_ascii_strncasecmp(const char *str1, const char *str2, size_t n);
functions.description: Case-insensitive ASCII string compare of at most n characters, locale-independent.
requirements: str1 and str2 should be non-NULL.
n specifies the maximum number of characters to compare.

functions.name: evutil_getaddrinfo
functions.signature: int evutil_getaddrinfo(const char *nodename, const char *servname, const struct evutil_addrinfo *hints_in, struct evutil_addrinfo **res);
functions.description: Libevent’s getaddrinfo clone for platforms without native getaddrinfo; otherwise maps to the system behavior. See RFC 3493 §6.1. Some flags (AI_V4MAPPED, AI_ALL) may not be implemented when emulated. For a nonblocking variant, use evdns_getaddrinfo.
requirements: res must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the result list on success; free it with evutil_freeaddrinfo().
hints_in may be NULL or point to a struct with fields per RFC 3493.
nodename and/or servname may be NULL depending on hints (as per getaddrinfo rules).
Returns 0 on success; on error, returns an EVUTIL_EAI_* code.

functions.name: evutil_freeaddrinfo
functions.description: Frees a result list returned by evutil_getaddrinfo or evdns_getaddrinfo.
requirements: ai must be a pointer returned from evutil_getaddrinfo or evdns_getaddrinfo (or NULL).

functions.name: evutil_gai_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string corresponding to an EVUTIL_EAI_* (or platform EAI_*) error code from evutil_getaddrinfo/evdns_getaddrinfo.
requirements: err should be an EVUTIL_EAI_* (or corresponding system EAI_*) error code.

functions.name: evutil_secure_rng_get_bytes
functions.description: Fills buf with n bytes of pseudorandom data from Libevent’s secure RNG. Current implementation is ARC4-based and not suitable for serious cryptographic applications.
requirements: buf must be a non-NULL pointer to at least n writable bytes.
Do not rely on this RNG for high-assurance cryptography.

functions.name: evutil_secure_rng_init
functions.description: Seeds the secure RNG if needed. Safe to call multiple times. Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
requirements: Callers may invoke multiple times; it returns 0 once seeded and -1 if seeding fails.

functions.name: evutil_secure_rng_set_urandom_device_file
functions.description: Overrides the device file used to seed the secure PRNG (replacing /dev/urandom). Must be called before any RNG initialization or use. The string is not copied internally and must remain valid while the RNG may be used. Intended only for real /dev/...random devices.
requirements: Must be called before calling any other RNG initialization or RNG functions.
fname must point to a valid, long-lived string path; it is not copied internally—do not free it while RNG users may run.
Only pass a real /dev/...random device file; using other files may reduce security.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: evutil_secure_rng_add_bytes
functions.description: Adds extra random bytes to the RNG state. Typically unnecessary if evutil_secure_rng_init() is used or the system provides arc4random(). If used as a replacement for normal entropy sources, the input must have strong entropy (hard to assure).
requirements: dat must point to a buffer of at least datlen bytes containing random data.
datlen specifies the number of bytes to read from dat.
On systems with arc4random(), this function is a no-op.

functions.name: evtag_init
functions.description: Initializes the tagged-data marshaling subsystem. Purpose: prepare any internal state needed for encoding/decoding tagged data in evbuffers. Usage: call before using other evtag_* APIs if required by the library; no parameters or return value.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time based on the header (no explicit ordering required is documented).
Thread-safety or idempotency is not documented; unknown.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_header
functions.description: Parses (unmarshals) the next tag header from evbuf and returns the payload length. Stores the tag ID in *ptag. Returns -1 on failure, or the number of bytes in the remaining payload on success. Use this to inspect the upcoming element before extracting its payload.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
ptag must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the tag id.
evbuf must have a complete, well-formed tag header at its current read position; otherwise the function returns -1.
Caller should handle a return value of -1 as an error.

functions.name: evtag_marshal
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t tag, const void *data, ev_uint32_t len);
functions.description: Writes a tagged field to evbuf consisting of the tag identifier and an arbitrary payload of length len bytes read from data. Intended for building tagged messages. Notes: The file comments state an assumption that tags are inserted in numeric order so unknown tags (higher numbers) can be ignored.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
If len > 0, data must point to at least len readable bytes.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order to preserve forward-compatibility.
Behavior for data == NULL with len > 0 is unspecified; avoid passing NULL unless len == 0.

functions.name: evtag_marshal_buffer
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal_buffer(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t tag, struct evbuffer *data);
functions.description: Writes a tagged field to evbuf where the payload is taken from another evbuffer (data). Useful for composing messages from existing buffers.
requirements: Both evbuf and data must be valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointers.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order.

functions.name: evtag_encode_int
functions.description: Encodes a 32-bit integer into evbuf using a nibble-based, byte-order-independent format. Purpose: low-level integer encoding for tagged data.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.

functions.name: evtag_encode_int64
functions.description: Encodes a 64-bit integer into evbuf using the same nibble-based, byte-order-independent format. Purpose: low-level integer encoding for tagged data.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.

functions.name: evtag_marshal_int
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal_int(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t tag, ev_uint32_t integer);
functions.description: Writes a tagged 32-bit integer field to evbuf. Encodes the integer in the library’s portable integer format and associates it with the given tag.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order.

functions.name: evtag_marshal_int64
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal_int64(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t tag, ev_uint64_t integer);
functions.description: Writes a tagged 64-bit integer field to evbuf. Encodes the integer in the library’s portable integer format and associates it with the given tag.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order.

functions.name: evtag_marshal_string
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal_string(struct evbuffer *buf, ev_uint32_t tag, const char *string);
functions.description: Writes a tagged string field to buf with the given tag. The exact on-wire format (e.g., length-prefixed vs. NUL-terminated) is not documented here; based on naming, it likely marshals a length-prefixed string.
requirements: buf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
string should be a valid NUL-terminated C string; passing NULL is not documented and should be avoided.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order.

functions.name: evtag_marshal_timeval
functions.signature: void evtag_marshal_timeval(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t tag, struct timeval *tv);
functions.description: Writes a tagged timeval structure to evbuf. Intended to serialize time values associated with a tag.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
tv must be a non-NULL pointer to an initialized struct timeval.
Tag insertion is assumed to be in increasing numeric order (as per file comment); callers should marshal tags in numeric order.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal(struct evbuffer *src, ev_uint32_t *ptag, struct evbuffer *dst);
functions.description: Extracts the next tagged field from src: stores its tag ID in *ptag and copies its payload into dst. Returns an integer status (exact return convention not specified here). Use evtag_unmarshal_header/peek to inspect beforehand if needed.
requirements: src and dst must be valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointers.
ptag must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the tag id.
src must contain a complete, well-formed tagged element at its read position.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success code is not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_peek
functions.description: Peeks at the next tag ID in evbuf without consuming the element, storing it in *ptag. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
ptag must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the tag id.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_peek_length
functions.description: Peeks at the payload length of the next tagged element in evbuf without consuming it, storing the length in *plength. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
plength must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the payload length.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_payload_length
functions.description: Returns the payload length for the next tagged element in evbuf and stores it in *plength. Function appears similar to evtag_peek_length; exact difference is not documented here.
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
plength must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the payload length.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_consume
functions.description: Consumes (skips over) the next tagged element in evbuf without returning its contents. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.
evbuf must contain a complete, well-formed tagged element at its current read position.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_int
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal_int(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t need_tag, ev_uint32_t *pinteger);
functions.description: Unmarshals a 32-bit integer from the next tagged element in evbuf, requiring the element to have tag need_tag. Stores the decoded integer into *pinteger. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
pinteger must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the integer.
The next element in evbuf must have tag equal to need_tag; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_int64
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal_int64(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t need_tag, ev_uint64_t *pinteger);
functions.description: Unmarshals a 64-bit integer from the next tagged element in evbuf, requiring the element to have tag need_tag. Stores the decoded value into *pinteger. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
pinteger must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the integer.
The next element in evbuf must have tag equal to need_tag; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_fixed
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal_fixed(struct evbuffer *src, ev_uint32_t need_tag, void *data, size_t len);
functions.description: Unmarshals a fixed-length payload from the next tagged element in src having tag need_tag into the caller-provided buffer data of length len. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: src must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
data must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len specifies the exact number of bytes expected; the tagged element’s payload must match this length.
The next element in src must have tag equal to need_tag; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_string
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal_string(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t need_tag, char **pstring);
functions.description: Unmarshals a string from the next tagged element in evbuf, requiring the element to have tag need_tag, and stores a pointer to the resulting C string in *pstring. Allocation/ownership details are not documented in this header and are unknown here. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
pstring must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting char*.
The next element in evbuf must have tag equal to need_tag; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.
Memory allocation and ownership for *pstring are not documented here; caller responsibilities for freeing are unknown.

functions.name: evtag_unmarshal_timeval
functions.signature: int evtag_unmarshal_timeval(struct evbuffer *evbuf, ev_uint32_t need_tag, struct timeval *ptv);
functions.description: Unmarshals a timeval structure from the next tagged element in evbuf, requiring the element to have tag need_tag, and writes it into *ptv. Returns an integer status (exact semantics not specified here).
requirements: evbuf must be a valid, initialized struct evbuffer pointer.
ptv must be a non-NULL pointer to a writable struct timeval.
The next element in evbuf must have tag equal to need_tag; otherwise the function fails.
Caller must check the return value and handle errors; exact success/failure codes are not specified in this header.

functions.name: event_enable_debug_mode
functions.description: Enables libevent’s internal debug mode, turning on extra consistency checks that fail early with assertions. Must be called before any events or event_bases are created. Useful to catch reassigning added events, or calling APIs on unassigned events.
requirements: Must be called before any events or event_bases are created.
May increase memory usage to track assigned-but-not-freed events; use event_debug_unassign() to stop tracking when appropriate.
Threading: call before any multithreaded use of Libevent.

functions.name: event_debug_unassign
functions.description: In debug mode, tells Libevent to stop tracking an event as assigned; no-op if debug mode is off. Use to reduce debug-mode memory usage.
requirements: The event must not be added (must be non-added).
The parameter must not be NULL.
Only meaningful if event_enable_debug_mode() was previously called.

functions.name: event_base_new
functions.description: Creates a new event_base for registering and dispatching events using default configuration.
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; caller must check return and handle errors.
The returned event_base must be freed with event_base_free() or event_base_free_nofinalize().
Only one thread may dispatch a given event_base at a time.

functions.name: event_reinit
functions.description: Reinitializes an event_base after a fork on platforms/backends that don’t survive across fork.
requirements: base must not be NULL.
Call only after fork() on a base that existed before the fork.
Returns 0 on success, -1 if some events could not be re-added; caller should handle failure (e.g., rebuild events).

functions.name: event_base_dispatch
functions.description: Runs the main dispatch loop until no events remain or until broken/exited. Convenience wrapper around event_base_loop().
requirements: base must not be NULL.
Return values: 0 on success; -1 on error; 1 if exited because no pending or active events.
Only one thread can be dispatching this base at a time.

functions.name: event_base_get_method
functions.description: Returns the name of the kernel event notification backend in use (e.g., kqueue, epoll, select).
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base pointer.
Returned pointer is owned by libevent; do not free.

functions.name: event_base_get_signal_method
functions.description: Returns the name of the signal handling mechanism in use ("signal", "kqueue_signal", or "signalfd_signal").
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base pointer.
String is libevent-owned; do not free.

functions.name: event_get_supported_methods
functions.description: Returns a NULL-terminated array of names for all compiled-in backends, ordered by preference. Does not verify OS support.
requirements: Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
Returned strings/array are libevent-owned; do not free.

functions.name: event_gettime_monotonic
functions.description: Queries the current monotonic time associated with an event_base into tp.
requirements: base and tp must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure; caller must check.
tp is filled on success.

functions.name: event_base_get_num_events
functions.signature: int event_base_get_num_events(struct event_base *eb, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Returns a count of events in the base, as specified by flags (EVENT_BASE_COUNT_ACTIVE, EVENT_BASE_COUNT_VIRTUAL, EVENT_BASE_COUNT_ADDED). Intended as an indication of workload only.
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base.
Flags is a bitwise combination of the supported EVENT_BASE_COUNT_* values.
Do not rely on exact values; semantics may change in future.

functions.name: event_base_get_max_events
functions.signature: int event_base_get_max_events(struct event_base *eb, unsigned int flags, int clear);
functions.description: Returns the maximum observed count of events in the base per the given flags; optionally clears the recorded maximum.
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base.
flags is a bitwise combination of EVENT_BASE_COUNT_* values.
clear controls whether the maximum is reset (nonzero clears).

functions.name: event_config_new
functions.description: Allocates a new event_config used to configure behavior of a new event_base before creation.
requirements: Returns NULL on error; caller must check.
Free with event_config_free() after use or after creating a base.

functions.name: event_config_free
functions.description: Frees an event_config and its resources.
requirements: cfg may be NULL or a valid pointer created by event_config_new().
Must not be used after freeing.
Does not free event_bases created with it.

functions.name: event_config_avoid_method
functions.description: Marks a backend method name to be avoided when creating an event_base.
requirements: cfg must be a valid event_config.
method must be a non-NULL method name string.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_base_get_features
functions.description: Returns a bitmask of features implemented by the base (EV_FEATURE_*).
requirements: base must be valid.
Caller interprets returned bitmask using enum event_method_feature.

functions.name: event_config_require_features
functions.description: Requires that the eventual event_base support the specified EV_FEATURE_* bitmask.
requirements: cfg must be valid.
feature is a bitfield of event_method_feature; replaces previously set requirements.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.
Caller must handle case where event_base_new_with_config() returns NULL if requirements cannot be met.

functions.name: event_config_set_flag
functions.description: Sets configuration flags (enum event_base_config_flag) to influence how the event_base will be initialized and operate.
requirements: cfg must be valid.
flag is a bitmask of event_base_config_flag values.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_config_set_num_cpus_hint
functions.description: Provides a CPU count hint for tuning thread pools (Windows/IOCP in 2.0).
requirements: cfg must be valid.
cpus should be a non-negative integer (inferred: count).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_config_set_max_dispatch_interval
functions.signature: int event_config_set_max_dispatch_interval(struct event_config *cfg, const struct timeval *max_interval, int max_callbacks, int min_priority);
functions.description: Configures limits on how many callbacks or how much time may elapse before polling for new events, optionally excluding lower priorities. Can reduce priority inversion at some throughput cost.
requirements: cfg must be valid.
max_interval may be NULL for no time limit.
max_callbacks >= -1; use -1 for no callback limit.
min_priority >= 0; 0 applies to all priorities.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_base_new_with_config
functions.description: Creates a new event_base honoring the supplied configuration (methods to avoid, required features, flags, etc.).
requirements: cfg may be NULL or a valid event_config pointer.
Returns NULL if no base can be created with the requested configuration; caller must handle.
Free the base with event_base_free() or event_base_free_nofinalize().

functions.name: event_base_free
functions.description: Frees an event_base and its internal resources, invoking any pending finalizer callbacks. Does not free user memory passed as callback arguments or close user fds.
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base or NULL (no-op behavior not specified; pass valid pointer).
Must not be used after freeing.
Pending finalizers will be invoked during free.

functions.name: event_base_free_nofinalize
functions.description: Frees an event_base without running finalizer callbacks.
requirements: Pointer must be a valid event_base created by event_base_new*().
After this call, the base is invalid.

functions.name: event_set_log_callback
functions.description: Installs a callback to receive libevent log messages (severity EVENT_LOG_DEBUG..EVENT_LOG_ERR). Passing NULL restores the default logger.
requirements: cb must not call any libevent function; doing so is undefined behavior.
Callback signature: void (*)(int severity, const char *msg).
Thread-safety of callback is up to the application.

functions.name: event_set_fatal_callback
functions.description: Overrides libevent’s default fatal-error handler (which calls exit(1)). The callback receives an error code; after invocation program state is undefined for further libevent calls.
requirements: cb should not rely on libevent being usable afterwards.
Callback signature: void (*)(int err).
Typically set early in program initialization.

functions.name: event_enable_debug_logging
functions.description: Globally enables or disables debug logging to the default log handler. Use EVENT_DBG_ALL to enable, EVENT_DBG_NONE to disable.
requirements: Must be called before creating any event_base and before multithreaded use.
Pass EVENT_DBG_ALL or EVENT_DBG_NONE as required parameter value.

functions.name: event_base_set
functions.description: Associates an existing event with a different event_base.
requirements: ev must not be currently active or pending.
eb and ev must be valid, non-NULL.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_base_loop
functions.description: Runs the dispatch loop with control flags (EVLOOP_ONCE, EVLOOP_NONBLOCK, EVLOOP_NO_EXIT_ON_EMPTY).
requirements: eb must be a valid event_base.
flags is a bitwise OR of EVLOOP_* flags.
Return values: 0 success; -1 error; 1 exited due to no pending/active events.
Only one thread may dispatch this base at a time.

functions.name: event_base_loopexit
functions.signature: int event_base_loopexit(struct event_base *eb, const struct timeval *tv);
functions.description: Requests the loop to exit after tv elapses; on expiry, the next loop iteration handles all queued events and then stops. NULL exits after processing currently active events.
requirements: eb must be valid.
tv may be NULL or a valid timeval pointer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_base_loopbreak
functions.description: Asks the active loop to abort immediately after the current event’s callback returns (like break).
requirements: eb must be valid.
Typically invoked from within an event callback.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_base_loopcontinue
functions.description: Asks the active loop to restart scanning for new events immediately after the current callback returns (like continue).
requirements: eb must be valid.
Has effect only if the loop is running.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_base_got_exit
functions.description: Checks whether loopexit has been requested on this base since last entering the loop.
requirements: eb must be valid.
Returns nonzero if event_base_loopexit() was called; 0 otherwise.

functions.name: event_base_got_break
functions.description: Checks whether loopbreak has been requested on this base since last entering the loop.
requirements: eb must be valid.
Returns nonzero if event_base_loopbreak() was called; 0 otherwise.

functions.name: event_self_cbarg
functions.description: Returns a sentinel value to pass as callback_arg to event_new()/event_assign() so the event pointer itself is provided to the callback.
requirements: Use only as the callback_arg in event_new()/event_assign().
The returned value must not be dereferenced or freed.

functions.name: event_new
functions.signature: struct event *event_new(struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t fd, short events, event_callback_fn callback, void *callback_arg);
functions.description: Allocates a new event configured to watch fd for specified events (EV_READ/EV_WRITE/EV_SIGNAL) and/or be triggered by timeout or manual activation. EV_PERSIST and EV_ET may be included. Returns an event to be added with event_add().
requirements: base must be a valid event_base.
If events includes EV_SIGNAL, fd must be a signal number; if no EV_READ/EV_WRITE/EV_SIGNAL, fd must be -1.
Multiple events on the same fd must all either use edge-triggered or all not edge-triggered.
On success, free with event_free(); returns NULL on error.
callback may be NULL only if you intend to activate and ignore; typically must be a valid function.

functions.name: event_assign
functions.signature: int event_assign(struct event *ev, struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t fd, short events, event_callback_fn callback, void *callback_arg);
functions.description: Initializes an already-allocated struct event to behave like event_new() would, without allocating memory.
requirements: ev must be a valid, allocated struct event.
ev must not be active or pending; calling on active/pending events will corrupt internal state.
base must be valid.
Argument semantics match event_new().
Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid arguments.

functions.name: event_free
functions.description: Deallocates an event allocated with event_new(). If pending/active, it is first made non-pending and non-active.
requirements: Pointer must be an event returned by event_new(); passing NULL is unspecified.
Do not use the event after freeing.

functions.name: event_finalize
functions.description: Schedules a finalize callback to run in the loop at the event’s priority, ensuring its callback is not running when tearing it down (multithread-safe teardown). Does not free the event.
requirements: Use with events created with EV_FINALIZE to avoid cross-thread blocking.
After calling, event_add() and event_active() will no longer work on the event; event_del() becomes a no-op.
Do not modify the event with event_assign()/event_set() while finalize callback runs.
The finalize callback must not add/activate events or attempt to resuscitate the finalized event.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_free_finalize
functions.description: Like event_finalize(), but frees the event automatically after the finalize callback runs.
requirements: Same constraints as event_finalize().
Caller must not access the event after finalization completes.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: event_base_once
functions.signature: int event_base_once(struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t fd, short events, event_callback_fn callback, void *arg, const struct timeval *timeout);
functions.description: Schedules a one-shot callback for the given fd/events or timeout without requiring an explicit event object.
requirements: base must be valid.
fd is -1 for timeout-only; events may be EV_READ, EV_WRITE, or EV_TIMEOUT.
timeout may be NULL: for EV_READ/EV_WRITE it waits forever; for EV_TIMEOUT it succeeds immediately (as documented note).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
In libevent 2.1, internal memory for an untriggered event is freed by event_base_free(); arg is never freed automatically.

functions.name: event_add
functions.signature: int event_add(struct event *ev, const struct timeval *timeout);
functions.description: Adds an event to the base, optionally with a timeout. If the event already has a scheduled timeout, this replaces it.
requirements: ev must have been initialized with event_new() or event_assign().
Must not call event_assign() on ev again until it is no longer pending.
timeout may be NULL for no timeout (wait forever).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_remove_timer
functions.description: Unschedules the timeout from a pending event without removing the event itself.
requirements: ev must be initialized via event_new()/event_assign().
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_del
functions.description: Removes an event from the set of monitored events, cancelling it if pending or active.
requirements: ev must not be NULL.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
No effect if the event has already executed or was never added.

functions.name: event_del_noblock
functions.description: Like event_del(), but never blocks waiting for the event’s callback to finish in another thread, even if EV_FINALIZE was not used.
requirements: ev must be valid.
Use event_finalize()/event_free_finalize() for safe teardown in multithreaded programs.
Returns int status like event_del().

functions.name: event_del_block
functions.description: Like event_del(), but always blocks until the event’s callback (possibly running in another thread) has finished, even if EV_FINALIZE was set.
requirements: ev must be valid.
May block; avoid calling from contexts where blocking is unsafe.
Returns int status like event_del().

functions.name: event_active
functions.signature: void event_active(struct event *ev, int res, short ncalls);
functions.description: Manually makes an event active so its callback will run during dispatch. Repeated calls OR the res flags together.
requirements: ev must be valid; can be pending or non-pending.
res is a bitmask of EV_* flags delivered to the callback.
ncalls is obsolete and ignored.

functions.name: event_pending
functions.signature: int event_pending(const struct event *ev, short events, struct timeval *tv);
functions.description: Checks whether an event is pending for any of the specified event types; optionally retrieves its timeout expiration time.
requirements: ev must be a valid event previously passed to event_add().
events is a bitmask of EV_TIMEOUT|EV_READ|EV_WRITE|EV_SIGNAL.
If tv is non-NULL and the event has a timeout, tv is set to the absolute expiration time.
Returns nonzero if pending on any requested types; 0 otherwise.

functions.name: event_base_get_running_event
functions.description: If called from within an event callback, returns that currently-running event for the given base.
requirements: Behavior is undefined if called from outside an event’s callback.
base must be the event_base currently dispatching the callback.

functions.name: event_initialized
functions.description: Heuristically tests whether a struct event might be initialized (distinguishes zeroed memory from initialized event).
requirements: ev must not be NULL.
Only reliable to distinguish zeroed memory from initialized; can be confused by uninitialized memory.

functions.name: event_get_fd
functions.description: Returns the fd or signal number associated with an event, or -1 if none.
requirements: ev must be valid.
For signal events, use event_get_signal(ev) macro for int signal number if desired.

functions.name: event_get_base
functions.description: Returns the event_base associated with an event.
requirements: ev must be valid.

functions.name: event_get_events
functions.description: Returns the EV_* flags assigned to an event (e.g., EV_READ, EV_WRITE, EV_SIGNAL, EV_PERSIST, EV_ET).
requirements: ev must be valid.

functions.name: event_get_callback
functions.description: Returns the callback function assigned to an event.
requirements: ev must be valid.

functions.name: event_get_callback_arg
functions.description: Returns the user callback argument assigned to an event.
requirements: ev must be valid.

functions.name: event_get_priority
functions.description: Returns the priority of an event.
requirements: ev must be valid.
Valid priorities are 0..(npriorities-1), where 0 is highest (per library behavior).

functions.name: event_get_assignment
functions.signature: void event_get_assignment(const struct event *event, struct event_base **base_out, evutil_socket_t *fd_out, short *events_out, event_callback_fn *callback_out, void **arg_out);
functions.description: Copies all constructor-time parameters of an event (base, fd, events, callback, arg) into provided output pointers.
requirements: event must be valid.
Any *_out argument may be NULL to ignore that field.

functions.name: event_get_struct_event_size
functions.description: Returns the size of struct event that the library was compiled with (may differ from application’s sizeof(struct event)).
requirements: Use to allocate compatible storage if avoiding event_new().
Value may be smaller than application’s sizeof(struct event) for ABI padding.

functions.name: event_get_version
functions.description: Returns a string with the runtime libevent version.
requirements: Returned string is library-owned; do not free.

functions.name: event_get_version_number
functions.description: Returns a packed numeric version (major, minor, patch in high three bytes; low byte unused).
requirements: Interpret using documentation; e.g., 0x02000100 for 2.0.1-alpha.

functions.name: event_base_priority_init
functions.description: Sets the number of event priorities for the base. Should be called before first dispatch. By default, all events get the middle priority.
requirements: eb must be valid.
npriorities is the maximum number of priorities; must be within library-supported range (up to EVENT_MAX_PRIORITIES).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.
Call before event_base_dispatch()/event_base_loop().

functions.name: event_base_get_npriorities
functions.description: Returns the number of different priorities configured on the base.
requirements: eb must be valid.

functions.name: event_priority_set
functions.description: Assigns a priority to an event.
requirements: ev must be valid.
priority must be in the configured range for the base (0..npriorities-1).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: event_base_init_common_timeout
functions.signature: const struct timeval *event_base_init_common_timeout(struct event_base *base, const struct timeval *duration);
functions.description: Optimizes scheduling for many timeouts with the same duration. Returns an opaque timeval pointer to pass to event_add() for faster handling.
requirements: base must be valid.
duration must be a valid timeval specifying the common interval.
Do not depend on the contents of the returned timeval; pass it unchanged to event_add().

functions.name: event_set_mem_functions
functions.signature: void event_set_mem_functions(void *(*malloc_fn)(size_t sz), void *(*realloc_fn)(void *ptr, size_t sz), void (*free_fn)(void *ptr));
functions.description: Overrides the malloc/realloc/free functions libevent uses for all allocations.
requirements: Call before any libevent function that does allocation, otherwise memory may be allocated with malloc() and freed with your free_fn (unsafe).
All memory returned from libevent must be freed with the provided free_fn if you replaced allocators.
Provide function pointers compatible with standard allocators.

functions.name: event_base_dump_events
functions.description: Writes a human-readable dump of all inserted/active events to the given FILE*. Intended for debugging; format is not stable.
requirements: base must be valid.
output must be a valid FILE* open for writing.

functions.name: event_base_active_by_fd
functions.signature: void event_base_active_by_fd(struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t fd, short events);
functions.description: Activates all pending events on the given fd with the specified mask on the base. Does not affect non-added events.
requirements: base must be valid.
fd must identify the target descriptor.
events is one or more of EV_{READ,WRITE,TIMEOUT}.

functions.name: event_base_active_by_signal
functions.description: Activates all pending events for the given signal number on the base. Does not affect non-added events.
requirements: base must be valid.
sig must be a valid signal number with pending events.

functions.name: event_base_foreach_event
functions.signature: int event_base_foreach_event(struct event_base *base, event_base_foreach_event_cb fn, void *arg);
functions.description: Iterates over all added or active events in the base, invoking fn for each. The callback must not modify the base or any events.
requirements: base must be valid.
fn must not call any function that modifies the event base or any event (including adding/removing). Violating this is unsupported and likely crashes.
Holds the base lock for the full iteration; callbacks should be fast.
Callback must return 0 to continue or nonzero to stop; function returns 0 if all visited, or callback’s value if stopped early.

functions.name: event_base_gettimeofday_cached
functions.description: Copies the event_base’s cached current time into tv, calling the system clock only if needed.
requirements: base and tv must be valid.
Returns 0 on success; negative on failure.
Cached time may be inaccurate during long callbacks.

functions.name: event_base_update_cache_time
functions.description: Updates the base’s cached current time to improve accuracy during long-running callbacks when time caching is enabled.
requirements: base must be valid.
Has effect only when in the event loop and when time caching is enabled (not disabled by EVENT_BASE_FLAG_NO_CACHE_TIME).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: libevent_global_shutdown
functions.description: Releases globally-allocated libevent resources (e.g., global locks). Optional; mainly for leak checkers. Should be called only when no further libevent calls will occur.
requirements: Call only once program is done using libevent; no libevent API should be called after this.
Does not free application-owned objects (event_bases, events, bufferevents, listeners, etc.).

functions.name: evbuffer_new
functions.description: Allocate and return a new evbuffer for efficiently buffering network data. Use evbuffer_free() to release it. Typically accessed via bufferevents (bufferevent_get_input/output).
requirements: Must be freed with evbuffer_free() when no longer needed.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; caller must check for NULL before use.

functions.name: evbuffer_free
functions.description: Deallocate an evbuffer and its storage.
requirements: buf must be a valid evbuffer pointer returned by evbuffer_new() or owned by the caller.
Do not use buf after calling this function (dangling pointer).

functions.name: evbuffer_set_max_read
functions.description: Set the maximum read buffer size for buf. Larger values can increase fragmentation/unfairness.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
max must be <= INT_MAX; otherwise function fails with -1.
Caller should consider performance implications before increasing the default (4096).
Return value must be checked for errors (-1).

functions.name: evbuffer_get_max_read
functions.description: Get the current maximum read buffer size associated with buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.

functions.name: evbuffer_enable_locking
functions.description: Enable internal locking on buf for safe multi-threaded use. If lock is NULL, a lock is allocated internally. When enabled, evbuffer callbacks are invoked with the lock held.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
If lock is non-NULL, it must be a valid lock object compatible with Libevent’s expectations (type unspecified here).
Beware of potential deadlocks: callbacks run with the buffer’s lock held; caller must avoid cycles.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_lock
functions.description: Acquire the lock on buf. No effect if locking has not been enabled via evbuffer_enable_locking().
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
Only meaningful if evbuffer_enable_locking() has been called on buf.
Calls should be paired with evbuffer_unlock() to avoid deadlock.

functions.name: evbuffer_unlock
functions.description: Release the lock on buf. No effect if locking has not been enabled via evbuffer_enable_locking().
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
Only meaningful if evbuffer_enable_locking() has been called on buf.
Must be called after a successful evbuffer_lock() to release the lock.

functions.name: evbuffer_set_flags
functions.description: Set one or more EVBUFFER_FLAG_* options on buf (additive).
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
flags must be a bitwise OR of EVBUFFER_FLAG_* values (e.g., EVBUFFER_FLAG_DRAINS_TO_FD).
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_clear_flags
functions.description: Clear (remove) one or more EVBUFFER_FLAG_* options from buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
flags must be a bitwise OR of EVBUFFER_FLAG_* values.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_get_length
functions.description: Return the total number of bytes currently stored in buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.

functions.name: evbuffer_get_contiguous_space
functions.description: Return the number of contiguous readable bytes available in the first chain of buf (0 if none).
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
Value may be less than total readable bytes if data spans multiple chains.

functions.name: evbuffer_expand
functions.description: Ensure buf has at least datlen bytes of additional space available without further allocations.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
datlen is the minimum additional capacity to guarantee; function may allocate more.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: evbuffer_reserve_space
functions.signature: int evbuffer_reserve_space(struct evbuffer *buf, ev_ssize_t size, struct evbuffer_iovec *vec, int n_vec);
functions.description: Reserve writable space at the end of buf and return one or more extents via vec for direct writing. Reserved space is not readable until committed via evbuffer_commit_space().
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
n_vec must be at least 1; 2 is more efficient.
vec must point to an array with at least n_vec elements to receive extents.
Caller must not perform any operation that moves the buffer’s internal memory before committing (i.e., between reserve and commit).
Multiple calls before commit will return the same extents.
The code currently returns no more than two extents (may change in future).
size is the minimum number of bytes requested; returned total may exceed size.
Return value is the number of extents provided, or -1 on error; caller must handle both.

functions.name: evbuffer_commit_space
functions.signature: int evbuffer_commit_space(struct evbuffer *buf, struct evbuffer_iovec *vec, int n_vecs);
functions.description: Commit some or all of the space previously reserved with evbuffer_reserve_space(), making it readable.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
vec must be the same extents returned by the preceding evbuffer_reserve_space().
n_vecs must match the number of extents being committed.
Only iov_len may be reduced to commit less than reserved; pointers must match.
No data may have been added to the buffer since reservation; otherwise commit fails.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error (e.g., mismatched extents or intervening modification).

functions.name: evbuffer_add
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add(struct evbuffer *buf, const void *data, size_t datlen);
functions.description: Append datlen bytes from data to the end of buf (copies data).
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
data must point to at least datlen valid bytes (non-overlapping with internal buffer).
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_remove
functions.signature: int evbuffer_remove(struct evbuffer *buf, void *data, size_t datlen);
functions.description: Copy up to datlen bytes from the start of buf into data and drain those bytes from buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least datlen bytes.
If fewer than datlen bytes are available, only that many are copied and drained.
Return value is bytes actually read, or -1 on error; caller must handle both cases.

functions.name: evbuffer_copyout
functions.signature: ev_ssize_t evbuffer_copyout(struct evbuffer *buf, void *data_out, size_t datlen);
functions.description: Copy up to datlen bytes from the start of buf into data_out without removing them from buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
data_out must point to a writable buffer of at least datlen bytes.
If fewer than datlen bytes are available, only that many bytes are copied.
Return value is bytes copied, or -1 on error; caller must handle negative return.

functions.name: evbuffer_copyout_from
functions.signature: ev_ssize_t evbuffer_copyout_from(struct evbuffer *buf, const struct evbuffer_ptr *pos, void *data_out, size_t datlen);
functions.description: Copy up to datlen bytes starting at position pos in buf into data_out without modifying buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
pos must be a valid position within buf (as obtained via evbuffer_ptr_set() or prior searches).
data_out must be a writable buffer of at least datlen bytes.
Return value is bytes copied, or -1 on error.

functions.name: evbuffer_remove_buffer
functions.signature: int evbuffer_remove_buffer(struct evbuffer *src, struct evbuffer *dst, size_t datlen);
functions.description: Move up to datlen bytes from src into dst, draining them from src. Avoids unnecessary copies.
requirements: src and dst must not be NULL and must be distinct buffers.
If src has fewer than datlen bytes, moves all available bytes.
