Return value is number of bytes moved.

functions.name: evbuffer_readln
functions.signature: char *evbuffer_readln(struct evbuffer *buffer, size_t *n_read_out, enum evbuffer_eol_style eol_style);
functions.description: Read one line from buffer, terminated by the specified EOL style, and return a newly allocated NUL-terminated string (EOL not included). Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
eol_style must be one of enum evbuffer_eol_style.
If n_read_out is non-NULL, it will be set to the number of characters in the returned string (can include NULs).
Returns NULL on error; caller must check before use and free non-NULL results.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_buffer
functions.description: Destructively move all data from inbuf to the end of outbuf without unnecessary copies; inbuf is emptied.
requirements: outbuf and inbuf must not be NULL and may be the same only if supported (not specified; treat as distinct).
After success, inbuf will be empty.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_buffer_reference
functions.description: Non-destructively copy data from inbuf into outbuf using internal references to avoid unnecessary copies.
requirements: outbuf and inbuf must not be NULL.
Buffers that already contain buffer references cannot be added to other buffers; caller must ensure inbuf is eligible.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_reference
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add_reference(struct evbuffer *outbuf, const void *data, size_t datlen, evbuffer_ref_cleanup_cb cleanupfn, void *cleanupfn_arg);
functions.description: Reference external memory [data, data+datlen) into outbuf without copying. The memory must remain valid until all referenced data has been read from outbuf. A cleanup callback is invoked when the reference is dropped.
requirements: outbuf must not be NULL.
data must point to at least datlen bytes that will remain valid until the buffer no longer references them.
cleanupfn may be NULL or a valid callback; it will be called with the original data pointer and length when no longer referenced.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_reference_with_offset
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add_reference_with_offset(struct evbuffer *outbuf, const void *data, size_t offset, size_t datlen, evbuffer_ref_cleanup_cb cleanupfn, void *cleanupfn_arg);
functions.description: Reference a subrange of external memory into outbuf without copying. Starts at data+offset and spans datlen bytes (offset excluded from datlen). Cleanup callback is invoked when no longer referenced.
requirements: outbuf must not be NULL.
data must point to a buffer of at least offset+datlen bytes that remains valid until reference is released.
offset and datlen define the referenced subrange; caller must ensure in-bounds.
cleanupfn may be NULL or a valid callback.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates error.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_file
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add_file(struct evbuffer *outbuf, int fd, ev_off_t offset, ev_off_t length);
functions.description: Efficiently add a file region to outbuf for writing to a socket, using sendfile or mmap where available. The function takes ownership of fd and will close it when finished (even on error). Reading bytes with evbuffer_remove/pullup on such data is undefined. For finer control, use file segments.
requirements: outbuf must not be NULL.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor; it will be closed by the function when finished transferring data (even on error).
offset is the file offset to start from.
length is the amount to read, or -1 to read as much as possible (requires fstat support on fd).
If EVBUFFER_FLAG_DRAINS_TO_FD is set and sendfile is available, sendfile-based operations may be used.
Caller must not rely on evbuffer_remove() or evbuffer_pullup() semantics for data added by this function (undefined).
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_file_segment_new
functions.signature: struct evbuffer_file_segment *evbuffer_file_segment_new(int fd, ev_off_t offset, ev_off_t length, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Create an evbuffer_file_segment referencing a file range for later addition to evbuffers (supports sendfile where available).
requirements: fd must be an open file descriptor referencing the file data.
offset is the file position at which the segment starts.
length is the length in bytes, or -1 to use as much as possible (requires fstat on fd).
flags is a bitmask of EVBUF_FS_* options (e.g., EVBUF_FS_CLOSE_ON_FREE, EVBUF_FS_DISABLE_MMAP, EVBUF_FS_DISABLE_SENDFILE, EVBUF_FS_DISABLE_LOCKING).
The fd must not be closed while any evbuffer is using this segment (unless using EVBUF_FS_CLOSE_ON_FREE to close on segment free).
Returns NULL on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: evbuffer_file_segment_free
functions.description: Free an evbuffer_file_segment. If the segment is still referenced by any evbuffer, it will be freed when no references remain.
requirements: seg may be NULL or a valid segment pointer; safe to call while referenced (actual free deferred).

functions.name: evbuffer_file_segment_add_cleanup_cb
functions.signature: void evbuffer_file_segment_add_cleanup_cb(struct evbuffer_file_segment *seg, evbuffer_file_segment_cleanup_cb cb, void* arg);
functions.description: Attach a cleanup callback to seg to be invoked when no more references to the segment exist.
requirements: seg must not be NULL.
cb must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with the segment, flags, and arg when segment is cleaned up.
arg is an opaque user pointer passed to cb.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_file_segment
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add_file_segment(struct evbuffer *buf, struct evbuffer_file_segment *seg, ev_off_t offset, ev_off_t length);
functions.description: Append some or all of seg to buf. Here, offset and length refer to the range within the segment (not the file).
requirements: buf and seg must not be NULL.
offset is the offset within seg (not the file).
length is bytes to add, or -1 to add the entire remaining segment.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_printf
functions.description: Append formatted text (printf-style) to buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string with corresponding arguments.
Return value is number of bytes added, or -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evbuffer_add_vprintf
functions.signature: int evbuffer_add_vprintf(struct evbuffer *buf, const char *fmt, va_list ap);
functions.description: Append formatted text using a va_list to buf (vprintf-style).
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; ap must be an initialized va_list.
Return value is number of bytes added, or -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evbuffer_drain
functions.description: Remove and discard len bytes from the start of buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
len is the number of bytes to remove; must not exceed available data for success (returns -1 on failure).
Return value must be checked.

functions.name: evbuffer_write
functions.description: Write the contents of buffer to fd, draining written bytes on success.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
fd must be a valid, writable socket or file descriptor appropriate for evutil_socket_t.
Return value is bytes written, or -1 on error; caller must check and handle partial writes.

functions.name: evbuffer_write_atmost
functions.signature: int evbuffer_write_atmost(struct evbuffer *buffer, evutil_socket_t fd, ev_ssize_t howmuch);
functions.description: Write up to howmuch bytes from buffer to fd, draining written bytes on success. If howmuch is -1, write as many bytes as possible.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
fd must be a valid, writable descriptor.
howmuch may be -1 to write as much as possible; otherwise should be >= 0.
Return value is bytes written, or -1 on error; caller must check and handle partial writes.

functions.name: evbuffer_read
functions.signature: int evbuffer_read(struct evbuffer *buffer, evutil_socket_t fd, int howmuch);
functions.description: Read up to howmuch bytes from fd into buffer. If howmuch is negative or exceeds per-read maximum, as many bytes as possible are read.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
fd must be a valid, readable descriptor.
howmuch may be negative to indicate 'as much as possible'.
Return value is bytes read, or -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evbuffer_search
functions.signature: struct evbuffer_ptr evbuffer_search(struct evbuffer *buffer, const char *what, size_t len, const struct evbuffer_ptr *start);
functions.description: Search for the first occurrence of the byte sequence [what, what+len) in buffer at or after start. Returns an evbuffer_ptr with pos set to the match offset, or -1 if not found.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
what must point to at least len bytes.
start may be NULL or a pointer to a valid evbuffer_ptr within buffer.

functions.name: evbuffer_search_range
functions.signature: struct evbuffer_ptr evbuffer_search_range(struct evbuffer *buffer, const char *what, size_t len, const struct evbuffer_ptr *start, const struct evbuffer_ptr *end);
functions.description: Search for the first occurrence of [what, what+len) in buffer between start and end. Returns an evbuffer_ptr with pos set to match offset, or -1 if not found.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
what must point to at least len bytes.
start may be NULL or a valid evbuffer_ptr indicating where to start.
end may be NULL or a valid evbuffer_ptr indicating where to stop.

functions.name: evbuffer_ptr_set
functions.signature: int evbuffer_ptr_set(struct evbuffer *buffer, struct evbuffer_ptr *ptr, size_t position, enum evbuffer_ptr_how how);
functions.description: Initialize or advance an evbuffer_ptr within buffer. With EVBUFFER_PTR_SET, set ptr to 'position' bytes from start; with EVBUFFER_PTR_ADD, advance ptr by 'position' bytes.
requirements: buffer and ptr must not be NULL.
If ptr is uninitialized, only EVBUFFER_PTR_SET is permitted.
Position may refer to any point from start up to immediately after end of buffer.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_search_eol
functions.signature: struct evbuffer_ptr evbuffer_search_eol(struct evbuffer *buffer, struct evbuffer_ptr *start, size_t *eol_len_out, enum evbuffer_eol_style eol_style);
functions.description: Search buffer for the next end-of-line sequence after start using the given EOL style. Returns an evbuffer_ptr with pos set to the EOL start, or -1 if not found. If eol_len_out is provided, it is set to the EOL length.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
start may be NULL or a valid evbuffer_ptr at which to begin searching.
eol_len_out may be NULL; otherwise will be set to EOL length on success.
eol_style must be one of enum evbuffer_eol_style.

functions.name: evbuffer_peek
functions.signature: int evbuffer_peek(struct evbuffer *buffer, ev_ssize_t len, struct evbuffer_ptr *start_at, struct evbuffer_iovec *vec_out, int n_vec);
functions.description: Inspect data in buffer without removing it by returning one or more extents via vec_out starting at start_at. If len is negative, try to fill as much of vec_out as possible; if len is negative and vec_out is NULL, return the number of extents needed for all data.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
start_at may be NULL (start of buffer) or a valid position within buffer.
If n_vec == 0, no pointers are returned; only the count of extents needed is computed.
vec_out must point to an array of at least n_vec evbuffer_iovec if n_vec > 0.
Return is number of extents needed; may be < n_vec (not all used) or > n_vec (more would be needed).

functions.name: evbuffer_add_cb
functions.signature: struct evbuffer_cb_entry *evbuffer_add_cb(struct evbuffer *buffer, evbuffer_cb_func cb, void *cbarg);
functions.description: Add a callback to buffer that is invoked whenever data is added or removed. Returns a handle for later removal. Passing cb == NULL removes all callbacks.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
cb may be NULL to remove all callbacks; otherwise must be a valid function pointer.
cb may add/remove itself or data, but may not remove another callback.
Callbacks may be invoked recursively if they modify buffers; caller must avoid infinite loops.
Return value must be checked; NULL indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_remove_cb_entry
functions.description: Remove a previously added callback using its handle; invalidates the handle.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
ent must be a valid handle returned by evbuffer_add_cb() and not already removed.
Return value must be checked: 0 if removed, -1 if not found.

functions.name: evbuffer_remove_cb
functions.signature: int evbuffer_remove_cb(struct evbuffer *buffer, evbuffer_cb_func cb, void *cbarg);
functions.description: Remove a previously added callback identified by function pointer and argument.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
cb and cbarg must match a previously added callback.
Return value must be checked: 0 if removed, -1 if not found.

functions.name: evbuffer_cb_set_flags
functions.signature: int evbuffer_cb_set_flags(struct evbuffer *buffer, struct evbuffer_cb_entry *cb, ev_uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Enable flags on a callback (e.g., EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED to re-enable a disabled callback).
requirements: buffer and cb must not be NULL.
flags must be a bitmask of callback flags (EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED).
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_cb_clear_flags
functions.signature: int evbuffer_cb_clear_flags(struct evbuffer *buffer, struct evbuffer_cb_entry *cb, ev_uint32_t flags);
functions.description: Disable flags on a callback (e.g., EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED to disable the callback).
requirements: buffer and cb must not be NULL.
flags must be a bitmask of callback flags (EVBUFFER_CB_ENABLED).
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_pullup
functions.description: Make the first size bytes of buf contiguous and return a pointer to the contiguous memory. If size is -1, make the entire buffer contiguous. Returns NULL if size exceeds available data.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
size may be -1 to request entire buffer; otherwise must be <= current length to succeed.
Operation may cause reallocation and copying; callers should prefer evbuffer_peek() if contiguity is not required.

functions.name: evbuffer_prepend
functions.signature: int evbuffer_prepend(struct evbuffer *buf, const void *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Prepend size bytes from data to the beginning of buf.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
data must point to at least size bytes.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_prepend_buffer
functions.signature: int evbuffer_prepend_buffer(struct evbuffer *dst, struct evbuffer* src);
functions.description: Prepend all data from src to the beginning of dst; src is emptied.
requirements: dst and src must not be NULL and should be distinct buffers.
After success, src will be empty.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_freeze
functions.description: Freeze buf to prevent modifications. If at_front is true, freeze the front (no draining/prepending); otherwise freeze the back (no appending).
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
While frozen at the front, operations that drain or prepend will fail; while frozen at the back, append operations will fail.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_unfreeze
functions.description: Unfreeze buf previously frozen with evbuffer_freeze(). If at_front is true, unfreeze the front; otherwise unfreeze the back.
requirements: buf must not be NULL.
Return value must be checked; -1 indicates failure.

functions.name: evbuffer_defer_callbacks
functions.description: Arrange for evbuffer callbacks on buffer to run from within the given event loop (base) instead of immediately after modifications. Useful for serializing callbacks to one thread.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
base should be a valid event_base associated with the desired event loop thread.
Return value must be checked; nonzero indicates failure (exact semantics unspecified).

functions.name: evbuffer_add_iovec
functions.signature: size_t evbuffer_add_iovec(struct evbuffer * buffer, struct evbuffer_iovec * vec, int n_vec);
functions.description: Append data from n_vec iovec entries to buffer, ensuring all appended data fits into a single chain for efficiency.
requirements: buffer must not be NULL.
vec must point to an array of at least n_vec valid iovec entries.
n_vec must be >= 1.
Return value is number of bytes successfully written.

functions.name: bufferevent_socket_new
functions.signature: struct bufferevent *bufferevent_socket_new(struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t fd, int options);
functions.description: Create a socket-based bufferevent bound to an event_base and (optionally) an existing nonblocking socket fd. Data written to the bufferevent is buffered and sent when possible; reads are buffered and delivered via callbacks.
requirements: base must not be NULL.
fd may be -1 (you must later set it via bufferevent_setfd() or bufferevent_socket_connect()).
fd must not be a pipe(2).
options is a bitmask of BEV_OPT_* values.
On success, the returned bufferevent must be freed with bufferevent_free().

functions.name: bufferevent_socket_connect
functions.signature: int bufferevent_socket_connect(struct bufferevent *bufev, const struct sockaddr *addr, int socklen);
functions.description: Initiate a nonblocking connect() on a socket-based bufferevent. If bufev has no socket yet, a nonblocking socket is allocated. On success, the event callback will eventually be invoked with BEV_EVENT_CONNECTED.
requirements: bufev must be a socket bufferevent created by bufferevent_socket_new().
addr points to the target address (may be NULL to indicate the socket is already connecting).
socklen is the size of the address structure pointed to by addr.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_socket_connect_hostname
functions.signature: int bufferevent_socket_connect_hostname(struct bufferevent *bufev, struct evdns_base *evdns_base, int family, const char *hostname, int port);
functions.description: Resolve a hostname and connect to it using a socket-based bufferevent. Optionally uses an evdns_base for asynchronous DNS; otherwise performs a blocking resolve. On success, BEV_EVENT_CONNECTED will be delivered via the event callback.
requirements: bufev must be a socket bufferevent created by bufferevent_socket_new().
evdns_base may be NULL (DNS resolution will block).
family must be AF_UNSPEC, AF_INET, or AF_INET6.
hostname must be a recognized hostname or IP literal (e.g., "www.example.com", "1.2.3.4", "::1", "[::1]").
port specifies the destination port.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_socket_connect_hostname_hints
functions.signature: int bufferevent_socket_connect_hostname_hints(struct bufferevent *bufev, struct evdns_base *evdns_base, const struct evutil_addrinfo *hints_in, const char *hostname, int port);
functions.description: Resolve a hostname using getaddrinfo-style hints and connect with a socket-based bufferevent. Can use evdns_base for asynchronous resolution; otherwise may block. Same behavior as bufferevent_socket_connect() after resolution.
requirements: bufev must be a socket bufferevent created by bufferevent_socket_new().
evdns_base may be NULL (DNS resolution may block).
hints_in points to addrinfo-style criteria used for address selection.
hostname must be a recognized hostname or IP literal (e.g., "www.example.com", "1.2.3.4", "::1", "[::1]").
port specifies the destination port.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_socket_get_dns_error
functions.description: Get the error code from the most recent failed DNS lookup performed by bufferevent_socket_connect_hostname().
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
Return value is a DNS error code suitable for evutil_gai_strerror().

functions.name: bufferevent_base_set
functions.description: Associate an existing socket bufferevent with a specific event_base.
requirements: Only supported for socket bufferevents.
base must be a valid event_base (e.g., from event_base_new()).
bufev must be a valid bufferevent created by bufferevent_new() or bufferevent_socket_new().
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_base
functions.description: Return the event_base associated with a bufferevent.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_priority_set
functions.description: Assign a priority to a socket-based bufferevent within the event loop.
requirements: Only supported for socket bufferevents.
bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
pri is an integer priority value (exact range depends on event_base configuration).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_priority
functions.description: Return the current priority of a socket-based bufferevent.
requirements: Only supported for socket bufferevents.
bufev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_free
functions.description: Deallocate and free a bufferevent and its resources. Pending output may not be flushed before free.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
Do not use bufev after calling this function.

functions.name: bufferevent_setcb
functions.signature: void bufferevent_setcb(struct bufferevent *bufev, bufferevent_data_cb readcb, bufferevent_data_cb writecb, bufferevent_event_cb eventcb, void *cbarg);
functions.description: Set the read, write, and event callbacks for a bufferevent, and the user-supplied callback argument pointer passed to each.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
readcb and writecb may be NULL to disable those callbacks.
eventcb may be NULL to disable the event callback.
cbarg is stored and passed to the callbacks.

functions.name: bufferevent_getcb
functions.signature: void bufferevent_getcb(struct bufferevent *bufev, bufferevent_data_cb *readcb_ptr, bufferevent_data_cb *writecb_ptr, bufferevent_event_cb *eventcb_ptr, void **cbarg_ptr);
functions.description: Retrieve the currently configured callbacks and callback argument from a bufferevent into the provided out-parameters.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
Each *_ptr parameter may be NULL; non-NULL pointers are set to the current values.

functions.name: bufferevent_setfd
functions.description: Change the file descriptor used by a bufferevent. Not supported by all bufferevent types.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent of a type that supports fd replacement.
fd is the new file descriptor to associate.
Existing descriptor (if any) is not closed by this function.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_replacefd
functions.description: Replace the file descriptor used by a bufferevent, closing the previous one if present. Not supported by all bufferevent types.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent of a type that supports fd replacement.
fd is the new file descriptor to associate.
This function closes the previous fd if any.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_getfd
functions.description: Return the file descriptor associated with a bufferevent, or -1 if none.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_underlying
functions.description: If bufev is a wrapper (e.g., a filtering or SSL bufferevent), return the underlying bufferevent; otherwise return NULL.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_write
functions.signature: int bufferevent_write(struct bufferevent *bufev, const void *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Append raw data to a bufferevent’s output buffer; it will be written to the fd when possible.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_write_buffer
functions.description: Transfer (drain) data from an evbuffer into a bufferevent’s output buffer without copying.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
buf must be a valid evbuffer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_read
functions.signature: size_t bufferevent_read(struct bufferevent *bufev, void *data, size_t size);
functions.description: Remove up to size bytes from a bufferevent’s input buffer and copy them into data.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
data must point to a writable buffer of at least size bytes.
Returns the number of bytes actually read (0 if no data available or read failed).

functions.name: bufferevent_read_buffer
functions.description: Transfer data from a bufferevent’s input buffer into an evbuffer without copying.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
buf must be a valid evbuffer to receive data.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_input
functions.description: Get the evbuffer used as the input buffer for a bufferevent. Do not set callbacks on this evbuffer.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
Caller must not set callbacks on the returned evbuffer.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_output
functions.description: Get the evbuffer used as the output buffer for a bufferevent. Do not set callbacks on this evbuffer. If filters are used and you manipulate the output buffer directly, you may need to manually trigger processing.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
Caller must not set callbacks on the returned evbuffer.
When filters are in use and the output buffer is manipulated directly, filters need to be manually triggered.

functions.name: bufferevent_enable
functions.description: Enable read and/or write events on a bufferevent.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
event is a combination of EV_READ and/or EV_WRITE.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_disable
functions.description: Disable read and/or write events on a bufferevent.
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
event is a combination of EV_READ and/or EV_WRITE.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_enabled
functions.description: Return a bitmask of currently enabled events (EV_READ | EV_WRITE) for a bufferevent.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_set_timeouts
functions.signature: int bufferevent_set_timeouts(struct bufferevent *bufev, const struct timeval *timeout_read, const struct timeval *timeout_write);
functions.description: Configure read and write timeouts. A timeout fires if the specified interval elapses while the bufferevent is actively attempting to read/write. On timeout, the corresponding operation is disabled and the event callback runs with BEV_EVENT_TIMEOUT | BEV_EVENT_READING/WRITING.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
timeout_read and timeout_write may be NULL to leave that direction unchanged/disabled.
Calling bufferevent_enable() or resetting timeouts resets pending timeouts.
Returns 0 on success.

functions.name: bufferevent_setwatermark
functions.signature: void bufferevent_setwatermark(struct bufferevent *bufev, short events, size_t lowmark, size_t highmark);
functions.description: Set low/high watermarks for read/write. Read callback fires only when at least lowmark bytes are buffered; reads pause when input exceeds highmark (may be overrun by some implementations). Write callback fires when output falls below lowmark; writers try not to exceed highmark (except on flush).
requirements: bufev must not be NULL.
events is EV_READ, EV_WRITE, or both.
lowmark and highmark are size thresholds for the specified directions.
High watermark may not be strictly enforced by some implementations (e.g., OpenSSL bufferevent).

functions.name: bufferevent_getwatermark
functions.signature: int bufferevent_getwatermark(struct bufferevent *bufev, short events, size_t *lowmark, size_t *highmark);
functions.description: Retrieve current low/high watermarks for either read or write.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
events must be exactly EV_READ or EV_WRITE (non-zero return if otherwise).
lowmark/highmark may be NULL; non-NULL outputs are assigned.
Returns 0 if events is EV_READ or EV_WRITE; nonzero otherwise.

functions.name: bufferevent_lock
functions.description: Acquire the lock protecting a bufferevent (only if created with BEV_OPT_THREADSAFE). No effect otherwise.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
Only has effect if BEV_OPT_THREADSAFE was set on creation.

functions.name: bufferevent_unlock
functions.description: Release the lock protecting a bufferevent (only if created with BEV_OPT_THREADSAFE). No effect otherwise.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
Only has effect if BEV_OPT_THREADSAFE was set on creation.

functions.name: bufferevent_incref
functions.description: Manually increment the reference count of a bufferevent so it won't be freed while externally referenced.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
Use with bufferevent_decref() to release the extra reference.

functions.name: bufferevent_decref
functions.description: Manually decrement the reference count of a bufferevent; frees it if the count reaches 0.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent and previously incref'd as appropriate.
Returns 1 if the bufferevent was freed, 0 otherwise.

functions.name: bufferevent_flush
functions.signature: int bufferevent_flush(struct bufferevent *bufev, short iotype, enum bufferevent_flush_mode mode);
functions.description: Ask a bufferevent to produce/flush more data for read and/or write paths according to the specified flush mode (BEV_NORMAL, BEV_FLUSH, BEV_FINISHED).
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
iotype is EV_READ, EV_WRITE, or both.
mode must be one of BEV_NORMAL, BEV_FLUSH, BEV_FINISHED.
Returns -1 on failure, 0 if no data was produced, 1 if data was produced.

functions.name: bufferevent_trigger
functions.signature: void bufferevent_trigger(struct bufferevent *bufev, short iotype, int options);
functions.description: Trigger read and/or write data callbacks on a bufferevent. Honors watermarks unless BEV_TRIG_IGNORE_WATERMARKS is set. If BEV_OPT_DEFER_CALLBACKS is set in options, callbacks are deferred.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
iotype is EV_READ, EV_WRITE, or both.
options may include BEV_TRIG_IGNORE_WATERMARKS and/or BEV_OPT_DEFER_CALLBACKS.

functions.name: bufferevent_trigger_event
functions.signature: void bufferevent_trigger_event(struct bufferevent *bufev, short what, int options);
functions.description: Trigger the event callback of a bufferevent with the given flag set (e.g., BEV_EVENT_TIMEOUT, BEV_EVENT_READING/WRITING, BEV_EVENT_CONNECTED). Can defer callbacks via BEV_OPT_DEFER_CALLBACKS.
requirements: bufev must be a valid bufferevent.
what is a bitmask of BEV_EVENT_* flags (and READING/WRITING context).
options may include BEV_OPT_DEFER_CALLBACKS.

functions.name: bufferevent_filter_new
functions.signature: struct bufferevent *bufferevent_filter_new(struct bufferevent *underlying, bufferevent_filter_cb input_filter, bufferevent_filter_cb output_filter, int options, void (*free_context)(void *), void *ctx);
functions.description: Create a filtering bufferevent layered over an existing underlying bufferevent. The input and/or output filters transform data between the layered bufferevent and its underlying transport. An optional free_context is called when the filter is freed.
requirements: underlying must be a valid bufferevent to wrap.
input_filter and/or output_filter may be NULL depending on direction of filtering desired.
options is a bitfield of BEV_OPT_* values.
free_context may be NULL; if non-NULL it must accept ctx.
ctx is passed to filter callbacks.
Returns a new bufferevent on success or NULL on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_pair_new
functions.signature: int bufferevent_pair_new(struct event_base *base, int options, struct bufferevent *pair[2]);
functions.description: Allocate a pair of linked bufferevents that communicate with each other like two ends of a socketpair, without creating actual sockets.
requirements: base must be a valid event_base.
options is a set of BEV_OPT_* flags.
pair must point to an array of two bufferevent* slots to receive the new bufferevents.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_pair_get_partner
functions.description: Given one bufferevent from a pair created by bufferevent_pair_new(), return the partner bufferevent if it still exists.
requirements: bev must be one of a pair created by bufferevent_pair_new().
Returns NULL if the partner no longer exists.

functions.name: ev_token_bucket_cfg_new
functions.signature: struct ev_token_bucket_cfg *ev_token_bucket_cfg_new(size_t read_rate, size_t read_burst, size_t write_rate, size_t write_burst, const struct timeval *tick_len);
functions.description: Create a token-bucket rate-limit configuration object specifying average rates and bursts for reading and writing, and the tick length used for accounting. Limits are best-effort.
requirements: read_rate/write_rate are average bytes per tick.
read_burst/write_burst are maximum bytes per single tick (must be <= EV_RATE_LIMIT_MAX).
tick_len may be NULL to use default (defaults to one second); sub-millisecond fractions are ignored.
Returns a new cfg on success or NULL on failure.
The returned cfg is not reference-counted; do not free while in use by any bufferevent/group.

functions.name: ev_token_bucket_cfg_free
functions.description: Free a token-bucket configuration created by ev_token_bucket_cfg_new().
requirements: cfg must not be freed while any bufferevent or group is still using it (not reference-counted).

functions.name: bufferevent_set_rate_limit
functions.description: Apply or remove a per-bufferevent token-bucket rate limit. If cfg is NULL, disables per-bev rate limiting. Only some bufferevent types currently enforce limits (socket-based and SSL-based).
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
cfg may be NULL to disable rate-limiting.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_new
functions.signature: struct bufferevent_rate_limit_group *bufferevent_rate_limit_group_new(struct event_base *base, const struct ev_token_bucket_cfg *cfg);
functions.description: Create a rate-limit group to constrain aggregate read/write across multiple bufferevents using the provided token-bucket configuration. Limits are best-effort.
requirements: base must be a valid event_base (used for group timers).
cfg must be a valid token-bucket configuration.
Returns a new group on success or NULL on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_set_cfg
functions.description: Change the rate-limiting configuration for an existing group.
requirements: group must be a valid group.
cfg must be a valid token-bucket configuration.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_set_min_share
functions.description: Set the minimum per-tick read/write allocation granted to any single bufferevent in the group, to reduce tiny-packet effects. Default is 64 bytes.
requirements: group must be a valid group.
min_share is the minimum quantum in bytes.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_free
functions.description: Free a rate-limit group. The group must be empty when freed.
requirements: group must have no member bufferevents at the time of call.

functions.name: bufferevent_add_to_rate_limit_group
functions.description: Add a bufferevent to a rate-limit group, constraining its aggregate read/write with other members. Passing g == NULL removes the bufferevent from its current group.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
A bufferevent can belong to at most one group at a time; if already a member, it is removed from the old group before being added to g.
g may be NULL to remove from any current group.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_remove_from_rate_limit_group
functions.description: Remove a bufferevent from its current rate-limit group, if any.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
Returns 0 on success (or if not in a group), -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_set_max_single_read
functions.description: Set the size limit for a single read operation for a bufferevent. Use 0 for a reasonable default.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
size is the maximum number of bytes to read per operation (0 selects a default).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_set_max_single_write
functions.description: Set the size limit for a single write operation for a bufferevent. Use 0 for a reasonable default.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
size is the maximum number of bytes to write per operation (0 selects a default).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_max_single_read
functions.description: Get the current size limit for a single read operation on a bufferevent.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
Returns a nonnegative size or 0/default value; type is ev_ssize_t.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_max_single_write
functions.description: Get the current size limit for a single write operation on a bufferevent.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
Returns a nonnegative size or 0/default value; type is ev_ssize_t.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_read_limit
functions.description: Return the current per-bufferevent read bucket size (remaining tokens). If no per-bev ratelimit is configured, returns EV_SSIZE_MAX. May be negative if the bev exceeded its limit.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_write_limit
functions.description: Return the current per-bufferevent write bucket size (remaining tokens). If no per-bev ratelimit is configured, returns EV_SSIZE_MAX. May be negative if the bev exceeded its limit.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_max_to_read
functions.description: Return the maximum number of bytes the bufferevent is currently willing to read, considering limits and watermarks.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_max_to_write
functions.description: Return the maximum number of bytes the bufferevent is currently willing to write, considering limits and watermarks.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.

functions.name: bufferevent_get_token_bucket_cfg
functions.description: Get the per-bufferevent token-bucket configuration currently applied to bev, if any.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
Returns a pointer to the cfg or NULL if none is set.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_get_read_limit
functions.description: Return the current read bucket size for a rate-limit group. May be negative if the group has been made to read more than its limit.
requirements: group must be a valid group.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_get_write_limit
functions.description: Return the current write bucket size for a rate-limit group. May be negative if the group has been made to write more than its limit.
requirements: group must be a valid group.

functions.name: bufferevent_decrement_read_limit
functions.description: Subtract bytes from a bufferevent’s read bucket; negative values add tokens. Crossing zero will suspend/resume reading as appropriate. Does not affect any group limits.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
decr may be negative to increase tokens.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on internal error.

functions.name: bufferevent_decrement_write_limit
functions.description: Subtract bytes from a bufferevent’s write bucket; negative values add tokens. Crossing zero will suspend/resume writing as appropriate. Does not affect any group limits.
requirements: bev must be a valid bufferevent.
decr may be negative to increase tokens.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on internal error.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_decrement_read
functions.description: Subtract bytes from a group’s read bucket; negative values add tokens. Crossing zero affects reading for group members as appropriate.
requirements: group must be a valid group.
decr may be negative to increase tokens.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on internal error.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_decrement_write
functions.description: Subtract bytes from a group’s write bucket; negative values add tokens. Crossing zero affects writing for group members as appropriate.
requirements: group must be a valid group.
decr may be negative to increase tokens.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on internal error.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_get_totals
functions.description: Retrieve cumulative bytes ever read and written by all bufferevents in a group.
requirements: grp must be a valid group.
total_read_out and total_written_out may be NULL; non-NULL pointers are assigned with totals.

functions.name: bufferevent_rate_limit_group_reset_totals
functions.description: Reset the cumulative bytes read/written counters for a group to zero.
requirements: grp must be a valid group.

functions.name: evconnlistener_new
functions.signature: struct evconnlistener *evconnlistener_new(struct event_base *base, evconnlistener_cb cb, void *ptr, unsigned flags, int backlog, evutil_socket_t fd);
functions.description: Create a new TCP connection listener on an already-created, already-bound socket file descriptor. Associates the listener with the given event_base and optionally registers a connection callback. If cb is NULL, the listener starts disabled until a callback is set. The backlog controls the listen() queue length; pass -1 for a library default or 0 if the socket is already listening. Note: the DEFERRED_ACCEPT option is not supported for this constructor; the incoming accepted sockets will be made nonblocking unless LEV_OPT_LEAVE_SOCKETS_BLOCKING is set.
requirements: base must point to a valid, initialized struct event_base.
fd must be a valid, bound TCP socket file descriptor.
fd must be nonblocking before calling this function.
If backlog is -1, a reasonable default is used; if backlog is 0, the socket is assumed to be already listening.
cb may be NULL; in that case the listener is treated as disabled until a callback is set later.
flags may include any LEV_OPT_* flags; LEV_OPT_DEFERRED_ACCEPT is not supported for this constructor (do not rely on it having any effect).
Caller should ensure the lifetime of ptr (user data) outlives the listener or any pending callbacks.
On platforms/uses where LEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE is needed, set it if the underlying socket must be closed when the listener is freed.

functions.name: evconnlistener_new_bind
functions.signature: struct evconnlistener *evconnlistener_new_bind(struct event_base *base, evconnlistener_cb cb, void *ptr, unsigned flags, int backlog, const struct sockaddr *sa, int socklen);
functions.description: Create and bind a new TCP listening socket to the provided address, then create an evconnlistener on it. Associates the listener with the given event_base and optional connection callback. If cb is NULL, the listener starts disabled until a callback is set. Supports LEV_OPT_* flags including deferred accept where available. The backlog controls the listen() queue length; pass -1 for a library default.
requirements: base must point to a valid, initialized struct event_base.
sa must point to a valid socket address matching the desired protocol family; socklen must be the length in bytes of *sa.
cb may be NULL; in that case the listener is treated as disabled until a callback is set later.
flags may include any LEV_OPT_* flags; LEV_OPT_DEFERRED_ACCEPT is supported where the platform provides it.
If backlog is -1, a reasonable default is used for listen().
The caller must ensure that ptr (user data) remains valid for the lifetime of the listener/callbacks.

If using IPv6/IPv4 behavior flags, note: LEV_OPT_BIND_IPV6ONLY requests IPv6-only; LEV_OPT_BIND_IPV4_AND_IPV6 requests dual-stack where supported; platform defaults vary (Windows enables V6ONLY by default).
If the listener must close its socket on free, set LEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE.

functions.name: evconnlistener_free
functions.description: Disable and deallocate the given listener, releasing associated resources. If LEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE was specified at creation, the underlying socket is also closed.
requirements: lev must be a valid pointer to an evconnlistener obtained from evconnlistener_new() or evconnlistener_new_bind().
lev must not be used after this call returns.
If LEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE was not specified at creation, the underlying socket remains open and is the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: evconnlistener_enable
functions.description: Re-enable a previously disabled listener so that it resumes accepting new connections. Intended to be called after creation with a NULL callback or after an explicit disable.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.
The listener must have a valid callback set before enabling, otherwise no accept-callbacks will be delivered.
Return value semantics are not documented here; by libevent convention this likely returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (inferred). Handle nonzero return as an error.

functions.name: evconnlistener_disable
functions.description: Stop listening for new connections on the given listener. The listener remains allocated and can be re-enabled later.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.
Expect an integer status return; by libevent convention this likely returns 0 on success and -1 on failure (inferred). Treat nonzero return as an error.

functions.name: evconnlistener_get_base
functions.description: Retrieve the event_base associated with the given listener. Useful for inspecting or interacting with the base managing the listener.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.

functions.name: evconnlistener_get_fd
functions.description: Return the underlying listening socket file descriptor for the given listener.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.
The returned descriptor remains owned by the listener; do not close it directly unless you created the listener without LEV_OPT_CLOSE_ON_FREE and have otherwise taken ownership.

functions.name: evconnlistener_set_cb
functions.signature: void evconnlistener_set_cb(struct evconnlistener *lev, evconnlistener_cb cb, void *arg);
functions.description: Change the connection-accepted callback and its user-data pointer for the listener. This can be used to set a callback for a listener that was created disabled (cb was NULL) or to replace an existing callback.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.
cb may be NULL; behavior when setting NULL via this function is not specified here (unknown whether it implicitly disables the listener).
arg (user data) must remain valid for the duration of any callback invocations.
Be aware that unless LEV_OPT_LEAVE_SOCKETS_BLOCKING was set at creation, accepted sockets delivered to cb are made nonblocking.

functions.name: evconnlistener_set_error_cb
functions.description: Set a callback to be invoked when the listener encounters a non-retriable error. Enables application-level handling or logging of listener failures.
requirements: lev must be a valid evconnlistener pointer.
errorcb may be NULL to clear the error callback.
The error callback will receive (listener, user_arg) where user_arg is the pointer supplied at listener creation.

functions.name: evdns_base_new
functions.description: Create and initialize an asynchronous DNS base tied to the given libevent event_base. It optionally initializes nameservers and other behaviors based on flags. Use this as the main handle for client-side DNS operations; free with evdns_base_free.
requirements: event_base must be a valid, initialized struct event_base pointer.
flags is a bitmask of EVDNS_BASE_INITIALIZE_NAMESERVERS | EVDNS_BASE_DISABLE_WHEN_INACTIVE | EVDNS_BASE_NAMESERVERS_NO_DEFAULT | EVDNS_BASE_NO_CACHE.
On failure, returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before using the result.

functions.name: evdns_base_free
functions.description: Shut down the asynchronous DNS resolver and terminate all active requests. If fail_requests is nonzero, in-flight requests complete with DNS_ERR_SHUTDOWN; otherwise they are silently discarded.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base created by evdns_base_new.
After calling, base is no longer valid.
If fail_requests != 0, callers of outstanding requests must be prepared to receive DNS_ERR_SHUTDOWN.

functions.name: evdns_base_clear_host_addresses
functions.description: Remove all hosts entries previously loaded into the evdns_base via evdns_base_load_hosts or evdns_base_resolv_conf_parse.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
This only affects hosts entries; it does not free the base.

functions.name: evdns_cache_write
functions.signature: void evdns_cache_write(struct evdns_base *dns_base, char *nodename, struct evutil_addrinfo *res, int ttl);
functions.description: Insert a record for nodename into the evdns cache with the provided addrinfo and TTL. Intended to prepopulate or override cache entries.
requirements: dns_base must be a valid evdns_base.
nodename must be a valid DNS name string (non-NULL).
res must point to a valid evutil_addrinfo result list.
ttl is in seconds. Exact valid range is not documented; nonnegative expected (inferred).

functions.name: evdns_cache_lookup
functions.signature: int evdns_cache_lookup(struct evdns_base *base, const char *nodename, struct evutil_addrinfo *hints, ev_uint16_t port, struct evutil_addrinfo **res);
functions.description: Lookup nodename in the evdns cache, producing an evutil_addrinfo result, honoring getaddrinfo-style hints and defaulting port fields to 'port'.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
nodename must be a non-NULL DNS name string.
hints follows getaddrinfo() semantics; may be NULL to indicate no hints.
port is used to fill result port numbers.
res must be a non-NULL out-parameter; on success, it receives an allocated result that the caller must free via evutil_freeaddrinfo.

functions.name: evdns_err_to_string
functions.description: Return a human-readable string explaining a DNS_ERR_* error code.
requirements: err should be one of the DNS_ERR_* constants; other values may return a generic description.

functions.name: evdns_base_nameserver_add
functions.signature: int evdns_base_nameserver_add(struct evdns_base *base, unsigned long int address);
functions.description: Add an IPv4 nameserver to the resolver by numeric address in network byte order (matching in_addr.s_addr).
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base and must not be NULL.
address must be an IPv4 address in network byte order.

functions.name: evdns_base_count_nameservers
functions.description: Return the number of configured nameservers (not necessarily running). Useful for verifying configuration.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.

functions.name: evdns_base_clear_nameservers_and_suspend
functions.description: Remove all configured nameservers and suspend pending resolves; they may be re-attempted after evdns_base_resume.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
Pending resolves will be suspended until evdns_base_resume is called; callers should resume to continue processing.

functions.name: evdns_base_resume
functions.description: Resume normal operation and re-attempt resolves left pending after evdns_base_clear_nameservers_and_suspend.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
Should be called after evdns_base_clear_nameservers_and_suspend to continue pending requests.

functions.name: evdns_base_nameserver_ip_add
functions.description: Parse an IPv4 or IPv6 address (optionally with :port or [IPv6]:port) and add it as a nameserver. Defaults to port 53 if unspecified.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base and must not be NULL.
ip_as_string must be a non-NULL string in one of the supported formats: [IPv6]:port, [IPv6], IPv6, IPv4:port, IPv4.

functions.name: evdns_base_nameserver_sockaddr_add
functions.signature: int evdns_base_nameserver_sockaddr_add(struct evdns_base *base, const struct sockaddr *sa, ev_socklen_t len, unsigned flags);
functions.description: Add a nameserver using a sockaddr address and length. Supports IPv4 or IPv6 depending on sa->sa_family.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
sa must point to a valid sockaddr (e.g., sockaddr_in or sockaddr_in6) for the nameserver address.
len must be the size of the structure pointed to by sa.
flags is currently unspecified; pass 0 unless documented otherwise.

functions.name: evdns_base_resolve_ipv4
functions.signature: struct evdns_request *evdns_base_resolve_ipv4(struct evdns_base *base, const char *name, int flags, evdns_callback_type callback, void *ptr);
functions.description: Start an asynchronous A-record lookup for name. On completion, invokes callback with DNS_IPv4_A results or an error. Returns a request handle for cancellation.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
name must be a DNS hostname string.
flags is 0 or a bitmask of DNS_QUERY_* flags (e.g., DNS_QUERY_NO_SEARCH, DNS_QUERY_USEVC, DNS_QUERY_IGNTC, DNS_CNAME_CALLBACK).
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with result, type, count, ttl, addresses (array of 4-byte IPv4 addresses), and ptr.
May return NULL on error; caller must check before using the handle.

functions.name: evdns_base_resolve_ipv6
functions.signature: struct evdns_request *evdns_base_resolve_ipv6(struct evdns_base *base, const char *name, int flags, evdns_callback_type callback, void *ptr);
functions.description: Start an asynchronous AAAA-record lookup for name. On completion, invokes callback with DNS_IPv6_AAAA results or an error. Returns a request handle for cancellation.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
name must be a DNS hostname string.
flags is 0 or a bitmask of DNS_QUERY_* flags.
callback must be a valid function pointer; it will be called with result, type, count, ttl, addresses (array of 16-byte IPv6 addresses), and ptr.
May return NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_base_resolve_reverse
functions.signature: struct evdns_request *evdns_base_resolve_reverse(struct evdns_base *base, const struct in_addr *in, int flags, evdns_callback_type callback, void *ptr);
functions.description: Start an asynchronous PTR-record lookup for an IPv4 address. On completion, invokes callback with a nul-terminated hostname string or an error.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
in must point to a valid struct in_addr with the IPv4 address.
flags is 0 or a bitmask of DNS_QUERY_* flags.
callback must be valid; it receives result, type=DNS_PTR, count, ttl, addresses (char* to hostname), and ptr.
May return NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_base_resolve_reverse_ipv6
functions.signature: struct evdns_request *evdns_base_resolve_reverse_ipv6(struct evdns_base *base, const struct in6_addr *in, int flags, evdns_callback_type callback, void *ptr);
functions.description: Start an asynchronous PTR-record lookup for an IPv6 address. On completion, invokes callback with a nul-terminated hostname string or an error.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
in must point to a valid struct in6_addr with the IPv6 address.
flags is 0 or a bitmask of DNS_QUERY_* flags.
callback must be valid; it receives result, type=DNS_PTR, count, ttl, addresses (char* to hostname), and ptr.
May return NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_cancel_request
functions.description: Cancel a pending DNS resolution request previously returned by a resolve function.
requirements: base must be the same evdns_base used to create req.
req must be a valid, in-flight request; behavior is undefined if already completed.

functions.name: evdns_base_set_option
functions.signature: int evdns_base_set_option(struct evdns_base *base, const char *option, const char *val);
functions.description: Set a configuration option on the DNS base. Supported options include ndots, timeout, max-timeouts, max-inflight, attempts, randomize-case, bind-to, initial-probe-timeout, max-probe-timeout, probe-backoff-factor, getaddrinfo-allow-skew, so-rcvbuf, so-sndbuf, tcp-idle-timeout, use-vc, ignore-tc, edns-udp-size. Options without values (use-vc, ignore-tc) should use an empty string or NULL for val.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base and must not be NULL.
option must be a valid option name (case per library convention).
val provides the value for the option; may be NULL/empty only for valueless options.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check return value.

functions.name: evdns_base_resolv_conf_parse
functions.signature: int evdns_base_resolv_conf_parse(struct evdns_base *base, int flags, const char *const filename);
functions.description: Parse a resolv.conf file and configure nameservers, search domains, and misc options according to the specified flags.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base and must not be NULL.
flags is a bitmask of DNS_OPTION_NAMESERVERS | DNS_OPTION_SEARCH | DNS_OPTION_MISC | DNS_OPTION_HOSTSFILE | DNS_OPTIONS_ALL | DNS_OPTION_NAMESERVERS_NO_DEFAULT.
filename must point to a resolv.conf-formatted file path.
On error, returns one of the EVDNS_ERROR_* codes; caller must check and handle.

functions.name: evdns_base_load_hosts
functions.description: Load an /etc/hosts-style file into the evdns_base. If hosts_fname is NULL, adds minimal localhost entries only. Only evdns_getaddrinfo uses these entries. Does not replace previously loaded entries.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
hosts_fname may be NULL for minimal localhost mapping; otherwise it must be a path to a hosts-format file.
To replace existing hosts entries, call evdns_base_clear_host_addresses first.
Returns 0 on success, negative on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_base_config_windows_nameservers
functions.description: Obtain and configure nameserver information from Windows system settings, preferring GetNetworkParams and falling back to the registry. Only implemented/available on Windows builds.
requirements: Must be compiled on Windows or with appropriate implementation macro; otherwise may be unavailable.
Takes a valid evdns_base pointer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_base_search_clear
functions.description: Clear the list of search domains configured on the evdns_base.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.

functions.name: evdns_base_search_add
functions.description: Append a domain to the list of search domains used when resolving names (subject to ndots behavior).
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
domain must be a non-NULL string representing a domain name.

functions.name: evdns_base_search_ndots_set
functions.signature: void evdns_base_search_ndots_set(struct evdns_base *base, const int ndots);
functions.description: Set the ndots parameter controlling when names are tried without search domains. If a name has >= ndots dots, it is tried as absolute first.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
ndots should be a nonnegative integer (range not explicitly documented).

functions.name: evdns_set_log_fn
functions.description: Set a callback to handle evdns log messages instead of the default libevent logging. The callback receives a warning flag and the message string.
requirements: fn may be NULL to restore default logging (inferred behavior is not explicitly documented).
Callback must be re-entrant with respect to potential logging contexts.

functions.name: evdns_add_server_port_with_base
functions.signature: struct evdns_server_port *evdns_add_server_port_with_base(struct event_base *base, evutil_socket_t socket, int flags, evdns_request_callback_fn_type callback, void *user_data);
functions.description: Create a UDP DNS server port using the given event_base and UDP socket. Incoming DNS requests on the socket invoke the provided callback; replies are constructed via evdns_server_request_add_* and sent with evdns_server_request_respond.
requirements: base must be a valid event_base.
socket must be a valid bound UDP socket suitable for receiving DNS queries.
flags must be 0 (no other values defined yet).
callback must be non-NULL; it will be invoked with struct evdns_server_request* and user_data.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check and close socket if needed.

functions.name: evdns_add_server_port_with_listener
functions.signature: struct evdns_server_port *evdns_add_server_port_with_listener(struct event_base *base, struct evconnlistener *listener, int flags, evdns_request_callback_fn_type callback, void *user_data);
functions.description: Create a TCP DNS server port using an existing libevent evconnlistener. Incoming TCP DNS connections and requests invoke the callback; build replies via evdns_server_request_add_* and send with evdns_server_request_respond.
requirements: base must be a valid event_base.
listener must be a valid evconnlistener configured to accept TCP connections.
flags must be 0 (no other values defined yet).
callback must be non-NULL.
Returns NULL on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_close_server_port
functions.description: Close a DNS server port created by evdns_add_server_port_with_base or evdns_add_server_port_with_listener and free associated structures.
requirements: port must be a valid server port created by the corresponding constructor.
After calling, port is no longer valid.

functions.name: evdns_server_port_set_option
functions.signature: int evdns_server_port_set_option(struct evdns_server_port *port, enum evdns_server_option option, size_t value);
functions.description: Configure options for a DNS server port. Currently supports setting maximum simultaneous TCP clients and TCP idle timeout (seconds).
requirements: port must be a valid evdns_server_port.
option must be one of: EVDNS_SOPT_TCP_MAX_CLIENTS, EVDNS_SOPT_TCP_IDLE_TIMEOUT.
These options apply only to TCP DNS servers.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_set_flags
functions.description: Set AA/RD (and related) flags in a reply being built for a DNS request.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request under construction.
flags is a bitmask including EVDNS_FLAGS_AA and/or EVDNS_FLAGS_RD.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_add_reply
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_add_reply(struct evdns_server_request *req, int section, const char *name, int type, int dns_class, int ttl, int datalen, int is_name, const char *data);
functions.description: Add a resource record to a DNS reply under construction. This low-level API allows specifying section, owner name, RR type/class, TTL, and raw RDATA (either name or data bytes).
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request currently being handled.
section must be one of EVDNS_ANSWER_SECTION, EVDNS_AUTHORITY_SECTION, or EVDNS_ADDITIONAL_SECTION.
name must be a non-NULL domain name string.
type and dns_class must be valid DNS RR type and class values (e.g., EVDNS_TYPE_*, EVDNS_CLASS_INET).
ttl is in seconds.
datalen must match the length of data provided.
is_name indicates whether data is a domain name (compressed) vs raw bytes.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_add_a_reply
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_add_a_reply(struct evdns_server_request *req, const char *name, int n, const void *addrs, int ttl);
functions.description: Convenience: add n IPv4 A records for the owner name to a reply under construction. addrs points to an array of n IPv4 addresses.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request.
name must be a non-NULL domain name string.
n must be the number of IPv4 addresses provided; must match the array length (inferred).
addrs must point to n IPv4 addresses (each 4 bytes, e.g., in_addr array) (inferred).
ttl is in seconds.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_add_aaaa_reply
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_add_aaaa_reply(struct evdns_server_request *req, const char *name, int n, const void *addrs, int ttl);
functions.description: Convenience: add n IPv6 AAAA records for the owner name to a reply under construction. addrs points to an array of n IPv6 addresses.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request.
name must be a non-NULL domain name string.
n must be the number of IPv6 addresses provided; must match the array length (inferred).
addrs must point to n IPv6 addresses (each 16 bytes, e.g., in6_addr array) (inferred).
ttl is in seconds.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_add_ptr_reply
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_add_ptr_reply(struct evdns_server_request *req, struct in_addr *in, const char *inaddr_name, const char *hostname, int ttl);
functions.description: Convenience: add a PTR record answer mapping an IPv4 address to a hostname in the reply under construction.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request.
in must point to the IPv4 address being reversed (may be used to form in-addr.arpa name).
inaddr_name may be provided explicitly; behavior when NULL is not documented.
hostname must be a non-NULL target hostname string.
ttl is in seconds.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_add_cname_reply
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_add_cname_reply(struct evdns_server_request *req, const char *name, const char *cname, int ttl);
functions.description: Convenience: add a CNAME record from owner name to cname in the reply under construction.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request.
name and cname must be non-NULL domain name strings.
ttl is in seconds.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_respond
functions.description: Send the constructed DNS response for a request and free the request structure. 'err' may include flags and/or error codes as part of the reply header.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request that has not yet been responded to or dropped.
After calling, req is freed/invalid.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_drop
functions.description: Free a DNS request without sending a reply.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request that has not yet been responded to or dropped.
After calling, req is freed/invalid.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error; caller must check.

functions.name: evdns_server_request_get_requesting_addr
functions.signature: int evdns_server_request_get_requesting_addr(struct evdns_server_request *req, struct sockaddr *sa, int addr_len);
functions.description: Retrieve the source address that made the DNS request into the provided sockaddr buffer.
requirements: req must be a valid evdns_server_request.
sa must point to a buffer large enough for the address; addr_len must specify its size.
Returns the number of bytes written on success; on failure returns -1 or a value greater than addr_len if the buffer is too small (inferred from similar APIs).

functions.name: evdns_getaddrinfo
functions.signature: struct evdns_getaddrinfo_request *evdns_getaddrinfo(struct evdns_base *dns_base, const char *nodename, const char *servname, const struct evutil_addrinfo *hints_in, evdns_getaddrinfo_cb cb, void *arg);
functions.description: Asynchronous getaddrinfo using the provided evdns_base. May invoke the callback immediately (returning NULL) if the result is available or invalid; otherwise returns a handle and calls cb later with getaddrinfo-style result and error code. Hosts-file entries are honored; various limitations apply as documented.
requirements: dns_base must be a valid evdns_base.
cb must be a valid callback; it receives (int result, struct evutil_addrinfo* res, void* arg).
nodename and/or servname follow getaddrinfo() rules; at least one should be non-NULL per getaddrinfo semantics (not explicitly restated here).
hints_in may be NULL or a valid evutil_addrinfo; limitations: AI_V4MAPPED and AI_ALL not implemented; ai_socktype supports only STREAM, UDP, or 0; ai_protocol supports only TCP, UDP, or 0.
If cache was for a different address family, callback may get EVUTIL_EAI_ADDRFAMILY with res = NULL.
If AI_CANONNAME is set but cached response lacks CNAME, cache is not used.
If result is immediately known, function invokes cb and returns NULL; caller must handle both cases.

functions.name: evdns_getaddrinfo_cancel
functions.description: Cancel an in-progress evdns_getaddrinfo request. Must not be called after its callback has been invoked. The callback will be invoked with EVUTIL_EAI_CANCEL.
requirements: req must be a valid, in-progress evdns_getaddrinfo_request.
Do not call after the callback has already run.

functions.name: evdns_base_get_nameserver_addr
functions.signature: int evdns_base_get_nameserver_addr(struct evdns_base *base, int idx, struct sockaddr *sa, ev_socklen_t len);
functions.description: Retrieve the address of the idx-th configured nameserver into sa.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
idx must be within the range of configured nameservers; otherwise returns -1.
sa must point to a buffer of size len; on success returns bytes written; on failure may return a value greater than len if buffer is too small.

functions.name: evdns_base_get_nameserver_fd
functions.description: Retrieve the file descriptor associated with the idx-th configured nameserver.
requirements: base must be a valid evdns_base.
idx must be within range of configured nameservers; otherwise returns -1.

functions.name: evhttp_new
functions.description: Create a new HTTP server bound to the provided event_base (or NULL to create one not tied to a base yet). Returns a new evhttp server handle, or NULL on error.
requirements: base may be NULL (optional)
On success, caller must later call evhttp_free() when no requests are being served

functions.name: evhttp_bind_socket
functions.signature: int evhttp_bind_socket(struct evhttp *http, const char *address, ev_uint16_t port);
functions.description: Bind the HTTP server to listen on the given address and TCP port. Can be called multiple times to bind additional ports.
requirements: http must be a valid evhttp* created by evhttp_new()
address must be a valid local IP address string
port is the TCP port to listen on
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure

functions.name: evhttp_bind_socket_with_handle
functions.signature: struct evhttp_bound_socket *evhttp_bind_socket_with_handle(struct evhttp *http, const char *address, ev_uint16_t port);
functions.description: Bind and return a handle object for the listening socket, allowing later reference/removal.
requirements: http must be valid
address must be a valid local IP address string
port is the TCP port to listen on
Returned pointer becomes invalid after http is freed
Returns NULL on failure

functions.name: evhttp_accept_socket
functions.description: Make the HTTP server accept connections on an already-created listening socket file descriptor. Useful with preforking or FD passing.
requirements: http must be valid
fd must be a socket ready for accept(2)

functions.name: evrpc_add_hook

functions.signature: int evrpc_resume_request(void *vbase, void *ctx, enum EVRPC_HOOK_RESULT res);

functions.name: evthread_set_lock_callbacks
functions.description: Registers a set of user-provided lock callbacks that Libevent will use for all internal locking. Must be called before any event_base is created to have effect. Typically not needed if using the built-in helpers (evthread_use_windows_threads/evthread_use_pthreads).

Thread support must not be disabled at build time (EVENT__DISABLE_THREAD_SUPPORT not defined) for this API to be available.

The provided struct evthread_condition_callbacks must have condition_api_version set to EVTHREAD_CONDITION_API_VERSION.

Callback pointers (alloc_condition, free_condition, signal_condition, wait_condition) must be valid and follow the documented contracts: signal_condition returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; wait_condition returns -1 on error, 0 when signalled, 1 on timeout.
wait_condition must release the associated lock while waiting and re-acquire it before returning; it must honor the optional timeout (NULL means wait indefinitely).
Thread support must not be disabled at build time for this API to be available.

requirements: id_fn must be a valid pointer to a function taking no arguments and returning an unsigned long identifying the current thread.
Should be called before creating any event_base so the base will use this callback.
The returned value from id_fn must uniquely identify a thread in the process context for the duration needed by Libevent.

functions.name: evthread_use_windows_threads

requirements: Must be called before any event_base is created for the base to use these primitives.
Only available if Libevent was built for Windows (EVTHREAD_USE_WINDOWS_THREADS_IMPLEMENTED defined); otherwise this symbol may be unavailable.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; callers should check the return value.

requirements: Must be called before any event_base is created for the base to use pthreads primitives.
Libevent must be built with pthreads support (EVTHREAD_USE_PTHREADS_IMPLEMENTED defined).

Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; callers should check the return value.

requirements: Must be called before any event_base is created for the base to use pthreads primitives.
Libevent must be built with pthreads support.
flags is a bitfield of EVTHREAD_PTHREAD_* values; unsupported flags are ignored or cause failure depending on implementation (not specified here).
Priority inheritance flag (EVTHREAD_PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT) takes effect only if pthread_mutexattr_setprotocol() is supported by the platform.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; callers should check the return value.

requirements: Must be called before any locks are allocated; otherwise behavior is unspecified or may not take effect.

requirements: base must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct event_base.
Should be called at most once per event_base; repeated calls are not documented (behavior unspecified).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on failure; callers must check the return value.
Safe to call from a signal handler or another thread only after successful initialization.

requirements: base must be a valid pointer to an initialized struct event_base.
callback must be a valid function pointer of type evwatch_check_cb.
The returned watcher is owned by the caller and should be released with evwatch_free when no longer needed (or it will be deallocated by event_base_free).
The callback receives the user-provided arg unmodified.

functions.name: evwatch_base
functions.description: Returns the event_base with which the specified watcher is registered. Useful for querying or coordinating with the associated event loop.
requirements: watcher must be a valid pointer to a watcher previously created (e.g., by evwatch_prepare_new or evwatch_check_new).

functions.description: Deregisters and deallocates the specified watcher. If not explicitly freed, watchers are eventually deallocated by event_base_free. Calling evwatch_free after its associated event_base has been freed is an error.

functions.description: Retrieves the backend’s expected polling duration (timeout) for the current loop iteration, as seen by a prepare callback. Writes the value into the provided timeval and returns 1 if available, otherwise returns 0 when no timeout applies (e.g., no pending EV_TIMEOUT or EVLOOP_NONBLOCK is set). Useful for comparing expected vs. actual poll durations.
requirements: info must be the contextual info pointer provided to an evwatch_prepare_cb (from within a prepare callback).
timeout must point to writable storage for a struct timeval when the caller wants to receive the timeout value.
The caller must check the return value and only read *timeout if the function returns 1 (indicating a value was written).

functions.name: evws_new_session

functions.description: Opens a new WebSocket session by upgrading an HTTP request to a WebSocket connection and registering a message callback. The callback (ws_on_msg_cb) is invoked on received frames: it is passed the connection, a frame type (e.g., WS_TEXT_FRAME or WS_BINARY_FRAME), a pointer to the payload, its length, and the user-supplied context (arg). For text frames, the payload is not NUL-terminated; if treating it as a C-string, the user must copy and add a terminating '\0'. Returns a newly initialized evws_connection on success or NULL on error. The options parameter is available but its specific flags/meanings are not described here (unknown).
requirements: req must be a valid struct evhttp_request corresponding to an HTTP request suitable for WebSocket upgrade (inferred from purpose).
The ws_on_msg_cb must be a valid function pointer compatible with: void (*)(struct evws_connection *, int type, const unsigned char *, size_t, void *).

If handling text messages as C-strings, the callback must copy the data and append a terminating '\0' before string-style use, or otherwise process without requiring NUL termination (stated in comments).
arg is an opaque user context pointer and will be passed back to the ws_on_msg_cb as provided.
options is an int; specific flag semantics are unknown from this header and should be treated as opaque.
On failure, the function returns NULL; callers must check for NULL before using the returned pointer.

functions.name: evws_send_text
